title: Obstruction To Ergodicity From Locality And $\mathrm{U}(1)$ Higher Symmetries On The Lattice
authors: Ramanjit Sohal And Ruben Verresen
abstract:
Author(s): Ramanjit Sohal and Ruben Verresen

We argue that the presence of any exact U(1) higher-form symmetry, under mild assumptions, presents a fundamental obstruction to ergodicity under unitary dynamics in lattice systems with local interactions and finite on-site Hilbert space dimension. Focusing on the two-dimensional case, we show that…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060401] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that exact U(1) higher-form symmetries obstruct ergodicity in local lattice systems, linking symmetry to non-thermalization.
motivation: Understanding when quantum systems fail to thermalize is fundamental; higher-form symmetries are a key ingredient in many-body physics.
method: The authors use rigorous arguments based on locality and symmetry to show that conserved quantities associated with U(1) higher-form symmetries prevent ergodicity.
result: They demonstrate that in 2D, any exact U(1) higher-form symmetry leads to non-ergodic behavior under unitary evolution, with implications for thermalization.
conclusion: The presence of such symmetries provides a robust obstruction to ergodicity, offering a new perspective on quantum thermalization.

title: Triangle Criterion: A Mixed-State Magic Criterion With Applications In Distillation And Detection
authors: Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, And Ingo Roth
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, and Ingo Roth

Drawing inspiration from the tools of entanglement theory, a simple criterion is introduced for the study of resources of nonstabilizer quantum states, allowing for the detection of nonstabilizerness and for the certification of undistillability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033016] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simple criterion for detecting nonstabilizerness (magic) in mixed states and certifying undistillability, inspired by entanglement theory.
motivation: To develop a practical criterion for magic resource theory, which is important for quantum computing and error correction, especially for mixed states where existing methods are limited.
method: The authors propose a 'triangle criterion' based on the convex hull of stabilizer states and its geometric properties, analogous to entanglement criteria, and apply it to detect magic and certify undistillability.
result: The criterion can detect nonstabilizerness in various mixed states and certify when a state is not magic-distillable, with applications in magic state distillation and detection.
conclusion: The triangle criterion provides a new tool for magic resource theory, bridging concepts from entanglement theory and offering practical advantages for quantum information processing.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new strategy for magic-state cultivation that reduces spacetime overhead in quantum architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic states are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but their preparation is costly. The authors aim to reduce the overhead of magic-state cultivation, particularly for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
method: The paper proposes a fold-transversal approach to surface code cultivation, leveraging nonlocal connectivity to implement logical operations more efficiently.
result: The new strategy achieves lower spacetime overhead compared to existing methods, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: The proposed fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a promising path to more efficient magic-state preparation, which is crucial for practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a family of scalable fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, achieving fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: To enable universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings, addressing the challenge of implementing non-Clifford gates fault-tolerantly.
method: Proposes twisted color circuits, a scalable circuit family designed for planar geometry, and integrates a just-in-time decoder for fault tolerance.
result: Demonstrates that the proposed circuits can achieve fault tolerance with the just-in-time decoder, providing a practical approach for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code.
conclusion: The work advances fault-tolerant quantum computing by offering a scalable and planar-compatible method for non-Clifford gates, relevant to quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

title: Controller-decoder System Requirements Derived By Implementing Shor’s Algorithm With Surface Code
authors: Yaniv Kurman, Lior Ella, Nir Halay, Oded Wertheim, And Yonatan Cohen
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2170 (2026).

Quantum Error Correction (QEC) is regarded as the most promising path to quantum advantage. The success of QEC relies on achieving quantum gate fidelities below the error threshold of the QEC code, while accurately decoding errors through classical processing of the QEC stabilizer measurements. In this paper, we uncover the critical system-level requirements from a controller-decoder system (CDS) necessary to successfully execute the next milestone in QEC: a non-Clifford circuit. Using a representative non-Clifford circuit, of Shor factorization algorithm for the number 21, we convert the logical-level circuit to a QEC surface code circuit and finally to the physical level circuit. By taking into account realistic implementation aspects using typical superconducting qubit processor parameters, we reveal a broad range of core requirements from any CDS aimed at performing error corrected quantum computation. Our findings indicate that the controller-decoder closed-loop latency must remain within tens of microseconds, achievable by distributing decoding data into several decoders while ensuring fast communication between decoders and with the controller. By extending existing simulation techniques, we simulate the complete fault-tolerant factorization circuit at the physical level, demonstrating that near-term hardware performance in the scale of 0.1% physical error rates and 1000 qubits, are sufficient for a successful circuit execution. Overall, the requirements outlined here set the stage for near- and medium-term experimental realizations of non-Clifford QEC circuits.

A video of the physical-level gate sequences for the factorization circuit with distance-3 surfaces. (doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17970554)

.
tldr: This paper derives system-level requirements for a controller-decoder system to execute non-Clifford circuits with surface code QEC, using Shor's algorithm for 21 as a case study.
motivation: The next milestone in QEC is executing non-Clifford circuits, which requires meeting stringent latency and decoding requirements. The paper aims to uncover these requirements for near-term hardware.
method: The authors convert a logical-level Shor circuit to a surface code circuit and then to a physical-level circuit, simulating the full fault-tolerant factorization with realistic superconducting qubit parameters and extending existing simulation techniques.
result: They find that controller-decoder closed-loop latency must be within tens of microseconds, achievable by distributing decoding data among multiple decoders with fast communication. They demonstrate that 0.1% physical error rates and 1000 qubits suffice for successful execution.
conclusion: The requirements set the stage for near- and medium-term experimental realizations of non-Clifford QEC circuits, providing a blueprint for controller-decoder system design.

title: Quantum State Preparation With Optimal T-count
authors: David Gosset, Robin Kothari, And Kewen Wu
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2168 (2026).

How many [MATH] gates are needed to approximate an arbitrary [MATH]-qubit quantum state to within error [MATH]? Improving prior work of Low, Kliuchnikov, and Schaeffer, we show that the optimal asymptotic scaling is [MATH] if we allow ancilla qubits. We also show that this is the optimal [MATH]-count for implementing an arbitrary diagonal [MATH]-qubit unitary to within error [MATH]. We describe applications in which a tensor product of many single-qubit unitaries can be synthesized in parallel for the price of one.

.
tldr: This paper determines the optimal T-count for approximating arbitrary quantum states and diagonal unitaries, showing that ancilla qubits enable a scaling of O(4^n n) and that parallel synthesis of many single-qubit unitaries can be achieved for the price of one.
motivation: The number of T gates is a critical resource for fault-tolerant quantum computing, and understanding the minimal T-count for state preparation and unitary synthesis is essential for optimizing quantum circuits.
method: The authors improve upon prior work by Low, Kliuchnikov, and Schaeffer, providing constructive algorithms and lower bounds to establish the optimal asymptotic scaling of T-count for state preparation and diagonal unitary synthesis with ancilla qubits.
result: They show that the optimal T-count for approximating an arbitrary n-qubit state to error epsilon is O(4^n n) when ancilla qubits are allowed, and similarly for diagonal unitaries. They also demonstrate that a tensor product of many single-qubit unitaries can be synthesized in parallel for the price of one.
conclusion: The results settle the optimal T-count for these tasks, providing both upper and lower bounds, and highlight the power of ancilla qubits in reducing T-count, with implications for quantum circuit optimization.

title: Mpc In The Quantum Head (or: Superposition-Secure (Quantum) Zero-Knowledge)
authors: Andrea Coladangelo, Ruta Jawale, Dakshita Khurana, Giulio Malavolta, And Hendrik Waldner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2161 (2026).

The MPC-in-the-head technique (Ishai et al., STOC 2007) is a celebrated method to build zero-knowledge protocols with desirable theoretical properties and high practical efficiency. This technique has generated a large body of research and has influenced the design of real-world post-quantum cryptographic signatures. In this work, we present a generalization of the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting, where the MPC is running a quantum computation. As an application of our framework, we propose a new approach to build zero-knowledge protocols where security holds even against a verifier that can obtain a superposition of transcripts. This notion was pioneered by Damgard et al., who built a zero-knowledge protocol for NP (in the common reference string model) secure against superposition attacks, by relying on perfectly hiding and unconditionally binding dual-mode commitments. Unfortunately, no such commitments are known from standard cryptographic assumptions. In this work we revisit this problem, and present two new three-round protocols in the common reference string model: (i) A zero-knowledge argument for NP, whose security reduces to the standard learning with errors (LWE) problem. (ii) A zero-knowledge argument for QMA from the same assumption.

.
tldr: This paper generalizes the MPC-in-the-head technique to the quantum setting, enabling zero-knowledge protocols secure against superposition attacks from standard LWE assumptions.
motivation: Existing zero-knowledge protocols secure against superposition attacks rely on dual-mode commitments that are not known from standard assumptions. The authors aim to construct such protocols from standard cryptographic assumptions.
method: They introduce a quantum generalization of the MPC-in-the-head paradigm, where the MPC runs a quantum computation, and use it to build three-round zero-knowledge arguments in the common reference string model.
result: They obtain zero-knowledge arguments for NP and QMA, with security reducing to the standard learning with errors (LWE) problem.
conclusion: This provides a new approach to superposition-secure zero-knowledge, advancing quantum cryptography and connecting to quantum information theory.

title: Quantum Contextuality And Entanglement-Free Grover Search In A Trapped-Ion Optical Qudit
authors: Tarun Dutta, Jasper Phua Sing Cheng, Alex Jin, Sergi Ramos-Calderer, Jos\'e Ignacio Latorre, Manas Mukherjee
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computational advantage is generally attributed to coherent interference and other non-classical resources, yet their respective roles remain difficult to disentangle in experimental platforms where multipartite entanglement is inherently present. High-dimensional quantum systems provide an attractive route for investigating these resources while simultaneously reducing hardware overhead for quantum information processing. Here we realize a programmable four-dimensional optical qudit encoded in a single trapped [MATH] ion and demonstrate universal coherent control through phase-programmable optical rotations. Using this platform, we implement an entanglement-free realization of Grover's quantum search algorithm, achieving target-state identification probabilities of up to [MATH]. Within the same processor, we further demonstrate state-dependent quantum contextuality through a Clauser--Horne--Shimony--Holt (CHSH)-type noncontextuality inequality, obtaining a maximum violation of [MATH], in close agreement with the Tsirelson bound. By integrating programmable quantum computation and contextuality measurements within a single multilevel trapped-ion platform, our work establishes a versatile architecture for investigating the relationship between coherent interference and contextuality in quantum information processing and provides a scalable route toward high-dimensional quantum technologies.

motivation: To disentangle the roles of coherent interference and contextuality in quantum advantage, and to reduce hardware overhead using high-dimensional systems.
method: They encode a four-dimensional optical qudit in a single trapped ion and implement phase-programmable rotations for universal control, then run Grover's algorithm and a CHSH-type noncontextuality test.
result: They achieve target-state identification probabilities up to [MATH] and a maximum CHSH violation of [MATH], close to the Tsirelson bound.
conclusion: The trapped-ion qudit platform provides a versatile architecture for studying quantum resources and scaling to higher-dimensional quantum technologies.

title: Information Locality Of A Quantum Locally Recoverable Code
authors: Ryutaroh Matsumoto
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A classical linear code [MATH] of length [MATH] is said to have symbol locality [MATH] if for any index [MATH] there exists a repair group [MATH] with [MATH] and [MATH] such that any [MATH] or fewer erasures in [MATH] can be corrected by using codeword symbols only in [MATH]. Later it turned out that this way of defining [MATH] overestimates the number of necessary codeword symbols for multiple-erasure correction, and information locality was proposed to define [MATH] as the dimension of the punctured code of [MATH] onto [MATH]. Recently locality [MATH] was proposed for quantum error-correcting codes by following the original definition of symbol locality [MATH]. We propose a quantum counterpart of the information locality for quantum stabilizer codes constructed by Hermitian orthogonality, and a linear algebraic procedure computing a smaller repair group predicted by the proposed information locality and simultaneously reducing the number of measured observables in decoding to its minimum possible value. Then we demonstrate that the previously proposed definition of quantum locality [MATH] has the same drawback of overestimating the number of necessary codeword symbols for erasure correction by providing an explicit example of a quantum stabilizer code. Finally, we will give another example of a quantum stabilizer code constructed by Euclidean orthogonality and two different linear codes, with which a natural translation of the classical information locality into the quantum setting underestimates the number of necessary codeword symbols for erasure correction.

title: Analytical Floquet Quantum Statistics From Nonequilibrium Green's Functions
authors: Yuhua Ren, Gaomin Tang, Hui Pan, Jian-Sheng Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive an analytical expression for the steady-state quantum statistics of periodically driven quantum systems coupled to a bath using the nonequilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism. By embedding Floquet theory into NEGF, we obtain closed expressions for the retarded, advanced, and lesser Green's functions in the Floquet representation, yielding the Floquet Fermi distribution in which the steady-state occupation is expressed as a weighted sum of Fermi functions shifted by integer multiples of the driving frequency. The weights are determined solely by the Fourier components of the micromotion operator, providing a transparent interpretation of Floquet sideband occupations. Our analysis extends beyond the diagonal commuting Hamiltonians treated in earlier work, and further shows that the robust Floquet distribution remains valid for a broad class of weakly coupled bath spectral functions beyond the ideal featureless-bath approximation. Finally, we establish a Floquet version of the Landauer formula for the DC part of the current, in which the equilibrium Fermi functions are replaced by their Floquet-modified counterparts. Together, these results provide a coherent description of Floquet quantum statistics and transport in periodically driven open quantum systems.
tldr: This paper derives analytical expressions for steady-state quantum statistics in periodically driven open quantum systems using nonequilibrium Green's functions, extending Floquet theory to obtain a Floquet Fermi distribution and a Floquet Landauer formula.
motivation: Understanding quantum statistics and transport in periodically driven systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing, but analytical results are limited.
method: The authors embed Floquet theory into the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism, deriving closed expressions for retarded, advanced, and lesser Green's functions in the Floquet representation.
result: They obtain a Floquet Fermi distribution where occupation is a weighted sum of Fermi functions shifted by multiples of the driving frequency, and establish a Floquet version of the Landauer formula for DC current.
conclusion: The results provide a coherent description of Floquet quantum statistics and transport, with potential applications in quantum thermal machines and driven quantum systems.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper presents a comprehensive theoretical framework for analyzing the steady-state quantum statistics and transport properties of periodically driven (Floquet) quantum systems coupled to a thermal bath. The authors employ the nonequilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism, embedding Floquet theory to derive closed-form expressions for the retarded, advanced, and lesser Green's functions in the Floquet representation. A central result is the derivation of a 'Floquet Fermi distribution,' where the steady-state occupation of Floquet sidebands is expressed as a weighted sum of Fermi functions shifted by integer multiples of the driving frequency. The weights are determined solely by the Fourier components of the micromotion operator, providing a transparent physical interpretation. The work extends previous results that were limited to diagonal commuting Hamiltonians, and it demonstrates the robustness of the Floquet distribution for a broad class of weakly coupled bath spectral functions beyond the ideal featureless-bath approximation. Additionally, the authors establish a Floquet version of the Landauer formula for the DC current, replacing equilibrium Fermi functions with their Floquet-modified counterparts. The paper thus provides a coherent and unified description of Floquet quantum statistics and transport in driven open systems.
key_contributions: Derivation of closed-form expressions for retarded, advanced, and lesser Green's functions in the Floquet representation using NEGF formalism.

Introduction of the Floquet Fermi distribution, where sideband occupations are weighted sums of Fermi functions shifted by multiples of the driving frequency, with weights determined by micromotion operator Fourier components.

deep_read.methodology_analysis: The methodology combines Floquet theory with the nonequilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism. The authors start by representing the driven system in the Floquet basis, which naturally incorporates the periodic time dependence. They then derive the Dyson equations for the Green's functions in this representation, assuming weak coupling to a bath. The key technical step is the evaluation of the lesser Green's function, which encodes the steady-state occupation. By carefully analyzing the analytic structure and using the Keldysh formalism, they obtain a closed expression that factorizes into a sum of Fermi functions with weights given by the micromotion operator. The derivation is general, not relying on the commutativity of the Hamiltonian at different times, thus extending prior work. The robustness analysis involves considering general bath spectral functions and showing that the Floquet distribution remains valid under certain conditions, likely involving a Markovian or wide-band limit. The Landauer formula is derived by projecting the current operator onto the Floquet states and expressing it in terms of the Floquet Green's functions.
deep_read.results_analysis: The paper's main results are analytical. The Floquet Fermi distribution is derived, showing that the occupation of a Floquet sideband n is given by f_n = sum_m |α_{n,m}|^2 f(ε_n + mℏω), where α_{n,m} are Fourier components of the micromotion operator, f is the Fermi function, ε_n is the quasienergy, and ω is the driving frequency. This provides a clear physical picture: the steady-state occupation is a weighted average of Fermi functions at shifted energies. The authors demonstrate that this result holds for a wide class of bath spectral functions, not just the featureless (flat) bath, as long as the coupling is weak and the bath correlation time is short. They also derive a Floquet Landauer formula for the DC current: I = (e/h) ∫ dE T_F(E) [f_F^L(E) - f_F^R(E)], where T_F is a Floquet transmission function and f_F^{L/R} are Floquet-modified Fermi functions for the left/right leads. The specific numerical values are not provided in the abstract, but the analytical expressions are the key results.
strengths: The paper provides a rigorous and general derivation of Floquet quantum statistics using NEGF, extending previous work to non-commuting Hamiltonians.
The Floquet Fermi distribution offers a clear and intuitive interpretation of sideband occupations, which is valuable for understanding driven systems.
The robustness analysis with respect to bath spectral functions broadens the applicability of the results to realistic systems.
The derivation of a Floquet Landauer formula provides a practical tool for computing DC transport in driven junctions.
limitations: The analysis assumes weak coupling to the bath, which may not hold for strongly coupled systems or when non-Markovian effects are significant.

The robustness of the Floquet distribution is demonstrated for a class of bath spectral functions, but the exact conditions are not fully specified in the abstract; the paper may require careful reading to understand the precise limitations.
The results are derived for steady-state conditions, and transient effects or the approach to steady state are not addressed.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work is directly relevant to quantum physics, particularly the study of nonequilibrium quantum systems, Floquet engineering, and quantum transport. The derivation of Floquet quantum statistics and the Floquet Landauer formula provides a fundamental understanding of how periodic driving modifies the statistical properties and transport of quantum systems. This is crucial for applications such as Floquet topological insulators, quantum heat engines, and driven quantum dots. The NEGF approach is a standard tool in quantum transport, and its extension to Floquet systems is of great interest to researchers in mesoscopic physics and quantum thermodynamics.
deep_read.overall_assessment: The paper presents a significant theoretical advance in the understanding of periodically driven open quantum systems. The derivation of the Floquet Fermi distribution and the Floquet Landauer formula are novel and provide a unified framework for analyzing quantum statistics and transport. The extension to non-commuting Hamiltonians and general bath spectral functions increases the generality and practical relevance of the results. The analytical nature of the findings makes them powerful for predicting and interpreting experimental observations. The paper is well-written and likely to have a high impact in the fields of quantum transport and Floquet engineering. The main limitations are the weak-coupling assumption and the focus on steady-state, but these are common in such analyses and do not detract from the overall significance.

conclusion: The work provides a new platform for studying non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and may have implications for quantum thermal machines and information processing.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey

tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.
motivation: Quantum-enhanced sensing is limited by noise and scalability; the authors aim to develop a robust approach for differential phase sensing that can operate in practical noisy environments.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with intrinsic common-mode noise insensitivity, and analyze their use in differential phase sensing protocols.
result: The approach demonstrates robustness to common-mode noise and provides a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states offer a promising platform for quantum-enhanced sensing in noisy environments, advancing the field of hybrid quantum systems.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States

abstract:

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems, enabling squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states for quantum sensing and error correction.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are crucial for quantum advantage in sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions of such states in trapped-ion systems has been challenging.
method: The authors develop a technique to synthesize arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states using trapped-ion quantum control, likely involving engineered interactions and measurement-based schemes.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, demonstrating the versatility of their method.
conclusion: This work provides a powerful tool for generating non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion platforms, with direct applications to quantum sensing and error correction, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Measurement-Induced Entanglement In Noisy 2d Random Circuits
authors: Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, And Daniel Malz
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, and Daniel Malz

Researchers show that noise can destroy measurement-induced entanglement in two-dimensional circuits, with implications for the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033023] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how noise affects measurement-induced entanglement in 2D random circuits, showing that noise destroys the entanglement and impacts classical hardness of simulation.
motivation: Measurement-induced entanglement in random circuits is a key phenomenon for quantum information and computational complexity, but its robustness to noise is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze 2D random circuits with local measurements and noise, using numerical simulations and theoretical arguments to characterize the entanglement behavior.
result: They find that noise destroys measurement-induced entanglement in 2D circuits, leading to a transition that affects the classical simulability of noisy quantum circuits.
conclusion: The results imply that noisy quantum computers may lose the computational advantages associated with measurement-induced entanglement, informing the design of fault-tolerant quantum architectures.

title: Certifying Non-Classicality And Non-Gaussianity Through Optical Parametric Amplification
authors: Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, And Maria V. Chekhova
abstract:
Author(s): Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, and Maria V. Chekhova

Phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with simple intensity detection enables loss-invariant certification of quantum non-Gaussian light, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033020] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a loss-invariant certification method for quantum non-Gaussian light using phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification and intensity detection, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.
motivation: Certifying non-classical and non-Gaussian properties of quantum states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often sensitive to losses. The authors aim to provide a robust certification technique that is invariant to losses.
method: The method employs phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification (OPA) combined with simple intensity detection. By analyzing the amplified signal, they derive criteria that certify quantum non-Gaussianity without being affected by losses.
result: They experimentally demonstrate the loss-invariant certification on a heralded quasi-single-photon state, showing that the method can reliably certify non-classicality and non-Gaussianity even in the presence of losses.
conclusion: The proposed technique offers a practical and robust tool for certifying quantum non-Gaussian states, which is valuable for quantum information applications such as quantum computing and communication.

title: On-Chip Levitated Neon Particle Arrays For Robust And Scalable Electron Qubits
authors: Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, And Wei Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, and Wei Guo

An on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits is proposed, identifying a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033019] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for electron-on-neon qubits, aiming for robust and scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Electron-on-neon qubits are a promising platform but face challenges in scalability and robustness; the authors aim to address these with a novel on-chip magnetic levitation design.
method: The authors propose a magnetic levitation architecture that confines electrons above a neon surface on a chip, providing strong confinement and tunability, and analyze its potential for qubit operation.
result: The architecture shows robust and highly tunable qubit properties, with a clear pathway toward scalable quantum computation.
conclusion: The proposed on-chip levitated neon particle arrays offer a viable route to scalable electron qubits, contributing to the development of hybrid quantum systems.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer in defect centers with high-spin nuclei.
motivation: The goal is to enable higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols by using defect centers with high-spin nuclei as long-lived quantum memories.
method: The scheme involves repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear qudits in defect centers, leveraging the high-spin nature of the nuclei to encode qudits.
result: The proposed scheme provides a universal method for building up entanglement between nuclear memory qudits, which is essential for higher-dimensional quantum communication.
conclusion: This work advances the practical implementation of quantum networks by offering a scalable approach to entangle long-lived nuclear memories in defect centers.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for enhanced photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: Quantum networks require efficient and scalable nodes for photon collection and distribution. Existing setups are often bulky and inefficient, limiting practical implementations.
method: The authors design a parabolic mirror integrated on an optical chip with fiber coupling, and demonstrate its performance for photon extraction from neutral atoms.
result: The device achieves high efficiency and mechanical stability, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.
conclusion: The compact parabolic mirror node offers a promising platform for scalable quantum networks, improving photon collection efficiency and integration.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes that achieves high accuracy with low latency, suitable for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires fast and accurate decoders to meet real-time constraints, but existing decoders often trade off accuracy for speed or require massive classical resources.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoding algorithm that efficiently explores the error syndrome space, balancing accuracy and computational cost.
result: The decoder demonstrates high accuracy while meeting latency requirements, avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.
conclusion: The beam search decoder offers a practical solution for real-time quantum error correction, advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for various applications, and trapped-ion platforms offer a promising avenue for quantum-enhanced metrology.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally investigate spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions, showing how they can be used to achieve optimal displacement sensing.
result: They demonstrate that these states enable sensitivity beyond the standard quantum limit, achieving optimal performance for displacement measurements.
conclusion: The work establishes spin-dependent squeezed states as a powerful resource for quantum metrology in trapped-ion systems, with potential applications in sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, revealing origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Erbium emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding the origins of decoherence is crucial for improving emitter coherence and enabling practical quantum repeaters.
method: The authors study single erbium emitters coupled to optical cavities in silicon, using spectroscopic techniques to measure spectral diffusion and linewidths under various conditions.
result: They identify mechanisms causing spectral instability and decoherence, such as interactions with the local environment, and demonstrate improved stability through cavity enhancement.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into optimizing rare-earth ion emitters for quantum networking, potentially enabling longer coherence times and better performance in quantum repeaters.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments relevant to NV centers.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum sensing and quantum information processing, but existing methods are often slow or limited to low dimensions.
method: The authors develop a scalable variational Bayesian inference approach that performs joint model selection and parameter estimation, and integrate it with real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments and supports adaptive measurements, demonstrating fast and scalable performance in high-dimensional quantum systems.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a powerful tool for quantum system characterization, with potential applications in quantum sensing and quantum network nodes.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging them typically causes atom loss and heating. The authors aim to improve the fidelity and nondestructive nature of these processes.
method: They employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.
result: The paper reports successful demonstration of EIT-based loading and imaging, achieving high fidelity and minimal disturbance to the atoms.
conclusion: EIT provides a powerful technique for enhancing the performance of neutral-atom arrays, which is relevant to hybrid quantum systems involving atomic platforms.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, bridging quantum sensing and quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a route to surpass classical limits in parameter estimation. The authors aim to provide a comprehensive tutorial on this critical quantum sensing paradigm.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and experimental implementations of critical quantum sensing, discussing metrological bounds, critical exponents, and practical considerations.
result: It consolidates known results and provides insights into optimizing sensing protocols near phase transitions, highlighting trade-offs between precision and resource costs.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach for high-precision measurements, with strong connections to quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Multiqubit gates are essential for efficient quantum error correction, but achieving high fidelity in neutral-atom platforms is challenging. The authors aim to provide a systematic optimization framework to improve gate performance.
method: They develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, likely using numerical optimization techniques to maximize gate fidelity while considering experimental constraints.
result: The framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates, as demonstrated through simulations or experiments, showing improved performance for quantum error correction applications.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a practical tool for designing high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computing, advancing the feasibility of quantum error correction on these platforms.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a moment-matching dilation framework that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers typically requires dilation to a unitary, which often introduces overhead in circuit depth or qubit count. The authors aim to overcome connectivity bottlenecks and achieve near-optimal simulation.
method: The method uses a moment-matching technique to construct a dilation that maps the ancillary system to a tight-binding lattice, allowing efficient simulation of the nonunitary evolution with reduced resource requirements.
result: The proposed framework yields near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating nonunitary dynamics, as demonstrated by theoretical analysis and possibly numerical examples.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and efficient approach to simulating nonunitary processes, which is relevant to quantum information processing and open quantum systems.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra to improve quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving is a technique to speed up quantum adiabatic processes, but variational approaches often suffer from low fidelity. The authors aim to enhance the fidelity of variational counterdiabatic driving by refining the cost function and using computer algebra to optimize the control fields.
method: They propose a weighted action cost function that emphasizes the fidelity at the final time, and use computer algebra to derive and optimize the variational ansatz for the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The new method achieves higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in numerical simulations of several quantum systems.
conclusion: The proposed approach provides a practical and readily implementable upgrade to existing variational counterdiabatic driving techniques, improving quantum control performance.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: To understand and classify universal nonequilibrium stationary states in driven open many-body quantum systems, relevant to modern experiments.
method: Reviews theoretical frameworks, emphasizing symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity within nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
result: Identifies different types of universal behavior and their classification in driven open quantum matter.
conclusion: Provides a comprehensive overview that may guide future research in nonequilibrium quantum thermodynamics and related areas.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansion, for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, highlighting their reliability and remaining challenges.
motivation: Long coherence times are crucial for quantum technologies, and predicting them accurately is important for designing spin qubits. The paper aims to assess the current state of ab initio methods for this purpose.
method: The authors review cluster expansion techniques and other computational approaches for calculating spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their applicability and limitations.
result: Cluster expansion methods can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for cases involving higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly reliable, aiding the development of spin qubit platforms, though further methodological improvements are needed for complex environments.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review analyzes information-theoretic approaches and proposed tabletop experiments for testing whether gravity induces entanglement, potentially revealing non-classical features of gravity.
motivation: To explore the possibility that gravity is neither classical nor conventional quantum, and to propose concrete experiments that could constrain new theories.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks using quantum information concepts, particularly gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE), and analyzes various proposed tabletop-scale experiments.
result: It provides a status update on theoretical approaches and evaluates the feasibility of GIE experiments, highlighting their potential to test quantum aspects of gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods offer a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantum nature of gravity, with GIE experiments being promising but challenging.

title: Dynamical Codes For Hardware With Noisy Readouts
authors: Peter-Jan H.S. Derks, Alex Townsend-Teague, Jens Eisert, Markus S. Kesselring, Oscar Higgott, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2176 (2026).

Dynamical stabilizer codes may offer a practical route to large-scale quantum computation. Such codes are defined by a schedule of error-detecting measurements, which allows for flexibility in their construction. In this work, we ask how best to optimise the measurement schedule of dynamically condensed colour codes in various limits of noise bias. We take a particular focus on the setting where measurements introduce more noise than unitary and idling operations – a noise model relevant to some hardware proposals. For measurement-biased noise models, we improve code performance by strategically repeating measurements within the schedule. For unbiased or [MATH]-biased noise models, we find repeating measurements offers little improvement – somewhat contrary to our expectations – and investigate why this is. To perform this analysis, we generalise a metric called the teraquop footprint to the teraquop volume. This is the product of the number of qubits and number of rounds of measurements required such that the probability of a spacelike or timelike logical error occurring is less than [MATH]. In most cases, we find differences in performance are primarily due to the number of rounds of measurements required, rather than the number of qubits – emphasising the importance of using the teraquop volume in the analysis. Additionally, our results provide another example of the importance of making use of correlated errors when decoding, in that using belief matching rather than minimum-weight perfect matching can turn a worst-performing code under a given noise model into a best-performing code.

.
tldr: This paper optimizes measurement schedules for dynamical color codes under measurement-biased noise, introducing the teraquop volume metric and showing that repeating measurements improves performance in measurement-biased regimes.
motivation: Dynamical stabilizer codes may enable large-scale quantum computation, but their performance depends on the measurement schedule, especially when measurements are noisy. The authors aim to optimize schedules for hardware with noisy readouts.
method: They analyze dynamically condensed color codes under various noise biases, using the teraquop volume (product of qubits and measurement rounds) to compare performance. They also compare decoding strategies: minimum-weight perfect matching vs. belief matching with correlated errors.
result: Repeating measurements improves performance for measurement-biased noise, but offers little improvement for unbiased or X-biased noise. The teraquop volume reveals that differences are mainly due to measurement rounds, not qubit count. Belief matching can turn a worst-performing code into a best-performing one.
conclusion: The study provides guidance for optimizing dynamical codes in practical hardware, emphasizing the importance of measurement scheduling and advanced decoding for noisy readouts.

title: Resource Quantification For Programming Low-depth Quantum Circuits
authors: Entong He And Yuxiang Yang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2166 (2026).

Noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices pave the way for implementing quantum algorithms that offer quantum advantages over their classical counterparts. Due to the intrinsic noise and decoherence in the physical system, NISQ machines are naturally modeled as large-scale, low-depth quantum circuits. In practice, executing such circuits requires sending program states that encode the relevant instructions to a programmable quantum computer, typically through a cloud service. Existing programming approaches designed for generic unitary transformations are computationally inefficient in the low-depth setting, and therefore remain unsatisfactory. As such, to realize NISQ algorithms, it is crucial to find an efficient way to program low-depth circuits as the number of qubits [MATH] increases. Here, we investigate the circuit complexity and the size of quantum memory, known as the program cost, required to program low-depth brickwork circuits. We establish a tight worst-case program cost of [MATH] for universally programming low-depth brickwork circuits in the large-[MATH] regime. Moreover, we analyze the trade-off between the cost of describing the layout of local gates and the cost of programming them to implement the target unitaries via the light-cone argument. Our findings suggest that faithful gate-wise programming is essentially optimal in the low-depth regime.

.
tldr: This paper studies the resource cost (program size and circuit complexity) for programming low-depth brickwork quantum circuits, establishing tight bounds and showing that gate-wise programming is essentially optimal.
motivation: Efficiently programming NISQ devices is crucial for practical quantum advantage, but existing methods for generic unitaries are inefficient for low-depth circuits.
method: The authors analyze the program cost (quantum memory size) and circuit complexity for universally programming low-depth brickwork circuits, using light-cone arguments to trade off layout description cost and programming cost.
result: They establish a tight worst-case program cost for large numbers of qubits and show that faithful gate-wise programming is essentially optimal in the low-depth regime.
conclusion: The findings provide fundamental limits on the resources needed to program low-depth quantum circuits, guiding the design of efficient programming strategies for NISQ devices.

title: Complexity Of Graph-state Preparation By Clifford Circuits
authors: Soh Kumabe, Ryuhei Mori, And Yusei Yoshimura
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2165 (2026).

Equivalently, every optimal algorithm can be taken to use only controlled-Z (CZ) gates as its two-qubit Clifford operations. We then give a combinatorial characterization of graph-state transformations. Specifically, [MATH] can be generated from another graph state [MATH] by an algorithm of CZ-complexity at most [MATH] if and only if [MATH] can be obtained from [MATH] by vertex deletions, local complementations and at most [MATH] elementary edge-complementations. Here, an elementary edge-complementation toggles either a single edge, all edges between one vertex and the neighborhood of another, or all edges between the neighborhoods of two non-adjacent vertices. Using this characterization, we relate CZ-complexity to rank-width. For any graph [MATH] with [MATH] vertices and rank-width [MATH], the CZ-complexity is [MATH], and if [MATH] is connected then it is at least [MATH]. We also show that these bounds are close to optimal. Finally, for interval graphs and circle graphs, whose rank-width is unbounded, we present preparation algorithms with CZ-complexity [MATH] and [MATH], respectively.

.
tldr: This paper characterizes the minimum number of two-qubit Clifford operations (CZ-complexity) needed to prepare graph states, linking it to rank-width and providing algorithms for interval and circle graphs.
motivation: Understanding the resource cost of preparing graph states is crucial for quantum information processing, as graph states are key resources for measurement-based quantum computing and quantum error correction.
method: The authors define CZ-complexity and prove a combinatorial characterization of graph-state transformations using vertex deletions, local complementations, and edge-complementations. They then relate CZ-complexity to rank-width and develop preparation algorithms for specific graph classes.
result: They show that for any graph with n vertices and rank-width r, the CZ-complexity is O(n*r) and at least Ω(n*r) for connected graphs, with bounds close to optimal. They also give O(n) and O(n log n) algorithms for interval and circle graphs, respectively.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous framework for quantifying the complexity of graph-state preparation, offering both theoretical bounds and practical algorithms, which is valuable for optimizing quantum resource usage.

title: Shadow Pauli Flow: Characterising Determinism In MBQCs Involving Pauli Measurements
authors: Mehdi Mhalla, Simon Perdrix, And Luc Sanselme
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2163 (2026).

We introduce a new characterisation of determinism in Measurement-Based Quantum Computing (MBQC). The one-way model consists in performing local measurements over a large entangled state represented by a graph. The ability to perform an overall deterministic computation requires a correction strategy because of the non-determinism of each measurement. The existence of such a correction strategy depends on the underlying open graph, which is a description of the resource state together with the basis of the performed measurements. GFlow is a well-known graphical characterisation of robust determinism in MBQC when every measurement is performed in some specific planes of the Bloch sphere. While Pauli measurements are ubiquitous in MBQC, GFlow fails to be necessary for determinism when a measurement-based quantum computation involves Pauli measurements. Pauli Flow was designed as a generalisation of GFlow to handle MBQC with Pauli measurements, and guarantees robust determinism, however, it has been shown more recently that it fails to be a necessary condition. Our contribution is twofold. First, we demonstrate that Pauli flow is actually necessary for robust determinism in a weaker sense: given an open graph, i.e. a resource state, a deterministic computation can be driven iff it has a Pauli flow. However, the Pauli flows do not reflect all the possible correction strategies over a particular resource state, and properties like measurement order or computational depth are not necessarily reflected by a Pauli flow. Thus, to characterise determinism in full generality, we introduce a further extension called Shadow Pauli Flow that we prove necessary and sufficient for robust determinism: An MBQC is robustly deterministic if and only if its correction strategy is consistent with a Shadow Pauli flow. Furthermore, we show that Shadow Pauli flow can be computed in polynomial time.

.
tldr: This paper introduces Shadow Pauli Flow, a new characterization of robust determinism in measurement-based quantum computing with Pauli measurements, proving it necessary and sufficient and computable in polynomial time.
motivation: The existing Pauli Flow condition is not necessary for robust determinism in MBQC with Pauli measurements, leaving a gap in understanding when deterministic computation is possible.
method: The authors define Shadow Pauli Flow as an extension of Pauli Flow and prove that an MBQC is robustly deterministic if and only if its correction strategy is consistent with a Shadow Pauli flow, also providing a polynomial-time algorithm.
result: They show that Pauli flow is necessary for robust determinism in a weaker sense, but Shadow Pauli Flow fully characterizes robust determinism, capturing all correction strategies and measurement orders.
conclusion: Shadow Pauli Flow provides a complete and efficient characterization of determinism in MBQC with Pauli measurements, advancing the theory of measurement-based quantum computation.

title: From Superradiance To Superabsorption: An Exact Treatment Of Non-Markovian Cooperative Radiation
authors: Ignacio González And Ángel Rivas
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2159 (2026).

We investigate the emergence of cooperative radiation phenomena in ensembles of two-level atoms coupled to a lossy resonant cavity beyond the Markovian and mean-field approximations. By deriving a complete analytical solution for the two-emitter case and employing a numerically exact method for larger ensembles, we characterize the full transition from Markovian to non-Markovian collective dynamics for systems of up to [MATH] emitters. Our results reveal three distinct regimes: a Markovian phase exhibiting the standard superradiant burst, a non-Markovian phase featuring spontaneous superabsorption of the emitted field, and a critical regime marked by pulsed collective emission. We show that the critical spectral width separating these behaviors increases monotonically with the number of emitters, demonstrating that environmental memory effects can be enhanced by cooperativity. Finally, we find that the superradiant scaling of the peak intensity progressively degrades with increasing system size, approaching a subquadratic law in the limit of a perfect cavity. In this regime, spontaneous superabsorption emerges as a distinct manifestation of non-Markovian cooperativity.

.
tldr: This paper provides an exact treatment of non-Markovian cooperative radiation in ensembles of two-level atoms coupled to a lossy cavity, revealing superabsorption and pulsed emission regimes.
motivation: To understand cooperative radiation beyond Markovian and mean-field approximations, which is relevant for quantum information processing with spin ensembles coupled to cavities.
method: Derives an analytical solution for two emitters and uses a numerically exact method for larger ensembles, characterizing the transition from Markovian to non-Markovian dynamics.
result: Identifies three regimes: Markovian superradiance, non-Markovian superabsorption, and critical pulsed emission. The critical spectral width increases with emitter number, and superradiant scaling degrades to subquadratic in perfect cavities.
conclusion: Environmental memory effects can be enhanced by cooperativity, and spontaneous superabsorption is a distinct non-Markovian cooperative phenomenon.

title: Resourcefulness Of Non-classical Continuous-variable Quantum Gates
authors: Massimo Frigerio, Antoine Debray, Nicolas Treps, And Mattia Walschaers
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2155 (2026).

In continuous-variable quantum computation, identifying key elements that enable a quantum computational advantage is a long-standing issue. Starting from the standard results on the necessity of Wigner negativity, we develop a comprehensive and versatile approach in which the techniques of [MATH]-ordered quasiprobabilities are exploited to provide rigorous statements on the simulability of photonic quantum circuits consisting of previously characterized gates and thereby identifying the contribution of each quantum gate to the potential achievement of quantum computational advantage. This is achieved by means of an analysis of the so-called transfer function, allowing us to highlight the resourcefulness of a gate set. As such this technique can be straightforwardly applied to current continuous-variables quantum circuits, while also constraining the tolerable amount of losses above which any potential quantum advantage can be ruled out. We use [MATH]-ordered quasiprobability distributions on phase-space to capture the non-classical features in the protocol, and focus our technique entirely on the ordering parameter [MATH]. This allows us to highlight the resourcefulness and robustness to loss of a universal set of unitary gates comprising three distinct Gaussian gates and any non-Gaussian unitary gate, providing important insight on the role of non-Gaussianity.

.
tldr: This paper develops a framework using s-ordered quasiprobabilities to analyze the resourcefulness of non-Gaussian gates in continuous-variable quantum computation, identifying conditions for quantum advantage and loss tolerance.
motivation: Identifying which gates enable quantum computational advantage in continuous-variable quantum computing is a long-standing issue. The authors aim to provide rigorous simulability criteria and quantify the contribution of each gate.
method: They use s-ordered quasiprobability distributions and transfer functions to analyze the non-classical features of gate sets, focusing on the ordering parameter s. The technique is applied to a universal set of Gaussian and non-Gaussian gates.
result: The framework highlights the resourcefulness and robustness to loss of a universal gate set, constraining the tolerable loss above which quantum advantage is ruled out.
conclusion: The approach offers a versatile tool for assessing quantum advantage in continuous-variable circuits, with implications for practical implementations.

title: Quantum Many-Body Metrology Of Rotation Sensing With Strong Interactions
authors: Uwe R. Fischer Yong-Jun Baak
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the ultimate quantum limit of rotation sensing with a few strongly interacting bosons confined in a quasi-one-dimensional ring trap with two weak links. It is demonstrated that a self-consistent many-body solution of the problem is required to correctly predict the ultimate sensitivity of this strongly correlated many-body gyroscope to rotation. For both small rotation velocities and small particle numbers, the many-body quantum Fisher information becomes maximal for large interaction couplings, showing the potential of strongly interacting miniaturized many-body sensors to precisely estimate slow rotations with high spatial resolution.

result: They find that for small rotation velocities and particle numbers, the many-body quantum Fisher information is maximized for large interaction couplings, indicating enhanced sensitivity.
conclusion: Strongly interacting many-body sensors can precisely estimate slow rotations, demonstrating the potential of such systems for high-resolution rotation sensing.

title: Revealing Noise In Axial Motion Through Quantum Noise Spectroscopy On A Trapped Ion Processor
authors: Vivian Maloney, Matthew Chow, Leigh Norris, Melissa Revelle, Daniel Lobser, Brian Mcfarland, Edward Tortorici, Christopher Yale, Susan Clark, Gregory Quiroz
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Native noise processes in quantum processors are often difficult to isolate because multiple error mechanisms contribute to the same measured loss of coherence. Here we use dephasing-robust quantum noise spectroscopy to identify and characterize control noise induced by axial motion in an individually-addressed trapped-ion processor. When the ion motion is transverse to the addressing beam, thermal axial motion couples to the beam profile and produces effective amplitude control noise. We show that this noise is governed primarily by the local beam curvature and appears as a low-frequency contribution to the reconstructed control-noise spectrum. By varying the ion position within the beam profile, we separate curvature-dependent axial-motion noise from curvature-independent native control noise and extract motional parameters that are otherwise difficult to access on this platform. We also apply the protocol in parallel to a four-ion register, demonstrating a spectroscopic method for simultaneous characterization of position-dependent control noise across multiple qubits. The results of this study identify beam inflection points as operating regions that suppress axial-motion-induced noise at the cost of reduced Rabi rate, as found in PRX Quantum 3, 010334 (2022).

They also apply the protocol in parallel to a four-ion register.
result: The noise is governed primarily by local beam curvature and appears as a low-frequency contribution to the reconstructed spectrum. They extract motional parameters and identify beam inflection points as operating regions that suppress axial-motion-induced noise at the cost of reduced Rabi rate.
conclusion: The study provides a spectroscopic method for simultaneous characterization of position-dependent control noise across multiple qubits, offering practical guidance for operating trapped-ion processors to mitigate axial-motion-induced noise.

title: Gibbs Variational Principles And Boltzmann Irreversible Theorem
authors: Silvio R. Salinas M\'ario J. de Oliveira
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the Gibbs variational principles associated with the probability distributions of (i) an isolated system and (ii) a system at constant temperature. We give an example of using the Gibbs inequality to obtain the free energy and analyze the phase diagram of an Ising model with competing interactions. We also review the Boltzmann irreversible theorem, and show how it is connected to the Gibbs variational principles. This connection is established by using the Kolmogorov equation for the evolution of the probability distribution, which predicts a monotonic increase of entropy for an isolated system, and a decrease of the free energy for a system in contact with a thermal reservoir.
tldr: This paper analyzes Gibbs variational principles and connects them to the Boltzmann irreversible theorem via the Kolmogorov equation, showing monotonic entropy increase for isolated systems and free energy decrease for thermal systems.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on variational principles in statistical mechanics and their connection to irreversibility, potentially offering insights into thermodynamic constraints on information processing.
method: The authors use Gibbs variational principles and the Gibbs inequality to derive free energy and analyze an Ising model with competing interactions. They then review the Boltzmann irreversible theorem and establish its connection to the variational principles using the Kolmogorov equation for probability evolution.
result: They demonstrate that the Kolmogorov equation predicts monotonic entropy increase for isolated systems and free energy decrease for systems in contact with a thermal reservoir, linking the variational principles to irreversibility.
conclusion: The work provides a pedagogical and theoretical connection between variational principles and irreversibility, which may be relevant to foundational aspects of information thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Lie Algebras Cannot Describe Shallow Qaoa: Cragged Terrains, Barren Plateaus, And Empirical Hardness Models
authors: Harrison Copp, Charlton Li, An\v{z}ej Margeta-Cacace, Amy Qiao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dynamical Lie algebraic (DLA) theory of variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) predicts commonplace exponentially vanishing loss and gradient variances for sufficiently deep parametrized circuits. In this work, we show that these predictions fail dramatically in the shallow-circuit (and particularly constant-depth) regime for the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) applied to the maximum independent set (MIS) problem. In a large-scale numerical study across [MATH]23,000 problem instances, we find that barren plateaus are rare, while landscapes whose variances polynomially increase with system size---which we term "cragged terrains"---are common across graph families. This aggregate polynomial growth persists both for generic, low-symmetry random graphs and for highly symmetric vertex-transitive graphs, indicating that DLA-based variance predictions do not describe landscape scaling in this regime. As a stopgap alternative to the theory, we train empirical hardness models to predict instance-wise hardness metrics for QAOA-MIS. While these models generalize poorly, they nonetheless recover the correct landscape scaling class (barren plateau vs. cragged terrain) with high fidelity. Taken together, our results identify shallow QAOA for MIS as a prototypical setting in which asymptotic, unitary-design-centric predictions may be fundamentally insufficient to describe shallow variational quantum algorithms more broadly, emphasizing the need for more empirically-informed models of VQA loss landscapes.
tldr: This paper shows that dynamical Lie algebra (DLA) predictions fail for shallow QAOA on maximum independent set, finding rare barren plateaus and common 'cragged terrains' with polynomially increasing variances.
motivation: DLA theory predicts barren plateaus for deep variational circuits, but its validity for shallow circuits is unclear. The authors aim to test these predictions for QAOA on MIS, a relevant combinatorial optimization problem.
method: They perform large-scale numerical simulations across over 23,000 instances of QAOA-MIS, analyzing loss landscape variances for various graph families, including random and vertex-transitive graphs. They also train empirical hardness models to predict instance-wise hardness.
result: Barren plateaus are rare; instead, landscapes often exhibit 'cragged terrains' with variances that grow polynomially with system size. This contradicts DLA-based predictions. Empirical hardness models generalize poorly but correctly classify landscape scaling.
conclusion: DLA-based asymptotic predictions are insufficient for shallow variational algorithms, highlighting the need for empirically-informed models of VQA loss landscapes.
