title: Competing Magnetic Order In EuPd 3 ...
authors: Michelle Ocker, Franziska Walther, Nour Maraytta, Matthieu Le Tacon, Michael Merz, Cornelius Krellner And Kristin Kliemt
abstract: Single crystals of EuPd Si were grown using a high-temperature EuPd-flux method. The material was structurally and chemically characterized by single-crystal x-ray diffraction, powder x-ray diffraction, Laue method and energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy. The structural analysis confirmed the orthorhombic crystal structure (space group ) but revealed differences in the lattice parameters and bond distances. The composition is close to the ideal 1:3:2 stoichiometry with an occupation of 7% of the Si sites by Pd. The heat capacity, electrical resistivity, and magnetic susceptibility show two magnetic transitions indicating magnetic ordering below 61 K and a spin reorientation at 40 K. The orthorhombic material shows magnetic anisotropy, with anisotropy constants and , for field applied along the three main symmetry axes, which is summarized in the temperature-field phase diagrams. The susceptibility data hint to an alignment of the magnetic moments along between and . Below the magnetic structure changes to an arrangement with moments canted away from . The single crystals investigated in this study are suggested to show antiferromagnetic order below instead of ferromagnetism that sets in at higher which might originate from certain differences in the structure, composition or defects that have an impact on the dominant coupling constants of the Ruderman–Kittel–Kasuya–Yosida interaction.
tldr: This paper characterizes the structural and magnetic properties of EuPd3Si2 single crystals, focusing on competing magnetic orders and anisotropy.
motivation: The study aims to understand the magnetic behavior of EuPd3Si2, which exhibits two magnetic transitions and potential antiferromagnetic order, to clarify the role of structural and compositional factors.
method: Single crystals were grown via a flux method and characterized using X-ray diffraction, EDX, heat capacity, resistivity, and magnetization measurements. Temperature-field phase diagrams were constructed.
result: The material shows orthorhombic structure with slight off-stoichiometry, two magnetic transitions at 61 K and 40 K, and magnetic anisotropy. Susceptibility suggests moment alignment along a-axis with a canted structure below 40 K.
conclusion: The observed antiferromagnetic order below 61 K may be influenced by structural differences and defects affecting RKKY interactions, providing insight into the magnetic phase diagram.

title: Moiré-driven Skyrmion Family
authors: Kuan He, Meng-Han Li, Shi-Da Fan, Zi-Bin Lin, Xiao-Ying Zhuang, Cheng-Lin Han, Li-Qun Chen, Zhao-Dong Xu, Xue-Feng Zhu And Tian-Zhi Yang
abstract: Skyrmion family members, including skyrmions, merons, and skyrmioniums, have been observed in diverse physical systems, yet their coexistence and transformation within a single controllable platform remain challenging. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a bilayer twisted moiré elastic system that enables the generation of multiple skyrmion family members with different topological charges. By constructing three-dimensional displacement vector fields, we establish a framework describing the evolution of topological invariants under twist-induced symmetry modulation, thereby governing controlled transitions and the stable coexistence of different skyrmion textures. In addition, manipulating the Lamb-wave phase introduces discontinuous transport of the topological textures, thereby revealing phason-like dynamics within the quasiperiodic structure. Together, these results provide a versatile route for controlling topological textures and open new possibilities for the design of integrated topological wave devices.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a bilayer twisted moiré elastic system that generates and controls multiple skyrmion family members with different topological charges, revealing phason-like dynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to achieve coexistence and transformation of different skyrmion textures within a single controllable platform, which has been challenging.
method: They construct a bilayer twisted moiré elastic system and use three-dimensional displacement vector fields to describe topological invariant evolution under twist-induced symmetry modulation. They also manipulate Lamb-wave phase to induce discontinuous transport.
result: They experimentally demonstrate generation of multiple skyrmion family members with different topological charges and controlled transitions, as well as phason-like dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a versatile route for controlling topological textures and opens possibilities for integrated topological wave devices.

title: From Understanding To Resonance: A Case Study Of Quantum Music And Embodied Science Communication
authors: Kenji Noda, Akira Koga, Stefan Heusler, Koji Hashimoto
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One challenge in science communication is how to engage audiences with highly abstract scientific fields often perceived as distant, technical, or inaccessible. This Practice Insight examines two initiatives implemented during the International Year of Quantum Science and Technology: Quantum Fest in Japan and Quantum100 in Germany, which together attracted more than 4000 participants. Both employed immersive artistic experiences, including music, visual art, and embodied participation to create alternative entry points into quantum physics. Drawing on post-event surveys, participant comments, and stakeholder interviews, this paper identifies three dimensions of resonance: sensory immersion and reduced psychological barriers, collective embodied meaning-making, and emerging transformative engagement. The findings suggest that resonance-driven approaches can complement explanation-centred science communication by enabling audiences to form meaningful relationships with science before, alongside, or beyond conceptual understanding.
tldr: This paper discusses science communication initiatives using music and art to engage the public with quantum physics, focusing on embodied resonance rather than technical content.
motivation: To address the challenge of making abstract scientific fields like quantum physics accessible and engaging to broad audiences.
method: The authors analyze two events (Quantum Fest in Japan and Quantum100 in Germany) using post-event surveys, participant comments, and stakeholder interviews to identify dimensions of resonance.
result: They identify three dimensions of resonance: sensory immersion, collective embodied meaning-making, and transformative engagement, which helped reduce psychological barriers.
conclusion: Resonance-driven approaches can complement explanation-centered science communication, enabling meaningful engagement with science beyond conceptual understanding.

title: Design Of A Thermal Loading Resilient Optical Enhancement Cavity For Operation At 515 Nm For X-ray Production Through Inverse Compton Scattering In An Energy Recovery Linac
authors: Alice Renaux (ijclab), Aurelien Martens (ijclab), Yann Peinaud (ijclab), Ronic Chiche (ijclab), Kevin Dupraz (ijclab), Marie Jacquet (ijclab), Daniele Nutarelli (ijclab), Fabian Zomer
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A fast and simple method to optimize a high-power optical enhancement cavity is proposed. It is applied to a four-mirror bow-tie cavity operating at 515 nm, which is to be implemented within the PERLE ERL for the production of X-rays through inverse Compton scattering. The optimized figure of merit is the expected X-ray photon rate. Thermal loading is carefully evaluated, giving also a path towards very high average power operation in infrared. One shows that photon rates exceeding 10^11 per second at average energies above 280 keV in apertures of a few miliradians are within reach. For easier comparison with existing Compact X-ray sources providing high rates of photons, the performance of the proposed design is also evaluated for a system delivering infrared laser pulses. It is shown that a source delivering more than 10^13 photons per second is achievable with this design, an unprecedented performance for existing Compton X-ray sources. The design procedure employed here can be easily applied to other applications of high-power high-finesse optical cavities.
tldr: This paper designs an optical enhancement cavity for X-ray production via inverse Compton scattering in an energy recovery linac, focusing on thermal loading resilience.
motivation: The authors aim to optimize a high-power optical cavity for a specific application (X-ray generation) in a particle accelerator context, which is outside the user's research interests.
method: They propose a fast optimization method for a four-mirror bow-tie cavity, evaluating thermal loading and optimizing the expected X-ray photon rate.
result: The design achieves photon rates exceeding 10^11 per second at >280 keV, and >10^13 photons per second in infrared, with unprecedented performance for Compton sources.
conclusion: The design procedure is generalizable to other high-power high-finesse cavities, but the work is primarily an engineering/optics design for accelerator-based X-ray sources.

title: A Dynamical Systems View Of Feedback Synthesis
authors: William Clark
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04172v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Control theory and dynamical systems are closely intertwined fields. Pontryagin's maximum principal offers a strong connection by providing a constructive way to synthesize feedback control laws via lifting the control system to a (Hamiltonian) dynamical system. Feedback laws can then be encoded as invariant manifolds of this induced dynamical system - under the condition that these manifolds project diffeomorphically back to the base control system. While feedback stabilization is impossible for many control systems, the above procedure can still be carried out. In this setting, the invariant manifold no longer projects diffeomorphically which results in the emergence of caustics. This paper offers an overview of the above connection by translating target sets from controls to isotropic submanifolds in symplectic geometry and associates feedback controllability to singularities of the induced invariant manifolds. Multiple low-dimensional examples are included to elucidate the theory.
tldr: This paper presents a dynamical systems perspective on feedback synthesis using symplectic geometry and Pontryagin's maximum principle.
motivation: The author aims to unify control theory and dynamical systems by encoding feedback laws as invariant manifolds, and to address cases where feedback stabilization is impossible.
method: The paper translates target sets to isotropic submanifolds in symplectic geometry and associates feedback controllability with singularities (caustics) of induced invariant manifolds, with low-dimensional examples.
result: It provides an overview of the connection between control systems and Hamiltonian dynamics, highlighting the emergence of caustics when manifolds do not project diffeomorphically.
conclusion: The work offers a geometric framework for feedback synthesis, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum networks.

title: Multimodal Alignment Through Joint Kernel Entropic Gromov--Wasserstein Optimal Transport
authors: Yixuan Florence Wu, Yilun Zhu, Naichen Shi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04234v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of aligning data from multiple modalities into a shared representation space, focusing on settings where strong pretrained unimodal encoders are available but cross-modal paired data are scarce. We propose a structure-preserving alignment framework, joint kernel entropic Gromov--Wasserstein Optimal Transport (JK-EGW), which maps multiple modalities into a common latent space by minimizing a quadratic optimal transport objective. JK-EGW leverages fine-grained similarity relationships within and across modalities to construct a global affinity kernel instead of relying on raw feature-space distances. Our framework naturally provides explicit control over the geometry and distribution of the latent embedding. On the theory side, we establish parametric sample complexity rate of [MATH], matching the corresponding rates for standard, entropic and Gromov--Wasserstein optimal transport. On the algorithmic side, we derive a scalable alternating procedure to solve JK-EGW with entropic optimal transport (EOT) updates through a low-rank kernel approximation and a variational lifting. This lifting scheme effectively relieves the burden of a quadratic objective, and allowing us to take the advantage of existing EOT solvers. Empirically, we focus on post-hoc alignment of embeddings from pretrained encoders in data-scarce regimes, and show that our proposed method achieves improved multimodal retrieval performance compared to existing alignment baselines.
tldr: This paper proposes a multimodal alignment method using optimal transport, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper addresses the problem of aligning data from multiple modalities with scarce paired data, leveraging pretrained encoders.
method: It introduces joint kernel entropic Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport (JK-EGW) to map modalities into a shared latent space, with a scalable alternating algorithm using low-rank kernel approximation and variational lifting.
result: The method achieves improved multimodal retrieval performance compared to existing baselines in data-scarce regimes.
conclusion: The paper contributes to machine learning and optimal transport, but has no connection to the user's research interests in quantum information science.

title: Dimension Rigidity And Projective Geometry Of Trace-Product Switchings Of The Gold Cube
authors: Oleksandr Kuznetsov
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We completely classify a natural scalar trace-product switching of the Gold almost perfect nonlinear function [MATH] in every even dimension. Nontrivial switchings occur only for [MATH]: the admissible coefficients are, respectively, the nonzero trace-zero elements, the six elements of multiplicative order nine, and [MATH]. For every even [MATH], no nonzero coefficient is admissible. The infinite range is excluded by additive-character estimates on a Fermat cubic, with exact finite bridges for [MATH]. The raw coefficient lists for [MATH] appeared earlier in Arshad's dissertation; our contribution is their intrinsic description, a proof uniform in the dimension, and the resulting dimension-rigidity theorem. We also classify normalized rank-two extensions in dimension eight by [MATH]. A binary trace selector accepts two coefficient values at each non-base projective point, and the eight accepted marked switchings form exactly two extended-affine, hence two CCZ, classes. A centre-independent low-rank derivative criterion reduces each rank-[MATH] candidate to [MATH] membership tests in precomputed forbidden sets. The global APN classes reached are known; the results describe their local organization around the Gold centre and rule out this switching mechanism in all larger even dimensions.
tldr: This paper classifies trace-product switchings of the Gold APN function in even dimensions, a topic in finite geometry and coding theory.
motivation: The paper aims to understand the structure of APN functions, which are important in cryptography, by classifying a specific switching operation.
method: The authors use additive-character estimates and finite field theory to classify admissible coefficients for the switching, with computational checks for small dimensions.
result: They find that nontrivial switchings occur only in dimensions 2, 4, and 6, and provide a dimension-rigidity theorem ruling out switchings in larger even dimensions.
conclusion: The results describe the local organization of APN classes around the Gold function and rule out this switching mechanism in higher dimensions, contributing to the classification of APN functions.

title: A Weighted Upwind Vector Kinetic Lattice Boltzmann Method For Hyperbolic Conservation Laws
authors: Michael W. Brown, Jehanzeb Chaudhry, John N. Shadid
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vector kinetic lattice Boltzmann (VKLB) methods have recently emerged as a promising framework for solving hyperbolic partial differential equation (PDE) systems. VKLB discretizes Boltzmann-type equations using a discrete set of lattice velocities, enforces discrete moment constraints, and carefully defines equilibrium distribution functions. In this work, we introduce novel upwinded equilibrium distribution functions constructed from conservation variables and numerical fluxes derived via continuous flux vector splitting based on the eigendecomposition of the flux Jacobian. This formulation enables the weighted-upwind VKLB equilibrium to be applied broadly to general hyperbolic systems. The method is verified on a set of challenging hyperbolic systems that includes the shallow water, Euler and ideal magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) equations. The proposed method demonstrates improved stability, reduced error norms, and sharper shock resolution across increasingly complex verification and benchmark problems.
tldr: This paper introduces a weighted upwind vector kinetic lattice Boltzmann method for solving hyperbolic conservation laws, with applications to shallow water, Euler, and MHD equations.
motivation: The authors aim to improve the stability and accuracy of vector kinetic lattice Boltzmann methods for general hyperbolic systems, which are important in computational fluid dynamics and plasma physics.
method: They construct upwinded equilibrium distribution functions using flux vector splitting based on the eigendecomposition of the flux Jacobian, and apply the method to several hyperbolic systems.
result: The method demonstrates improved stability, reduced error norms, and sharper shock resolution on benchmark problems.
conclusion: The proposed method is a promising numerical technique for hyperbolic conservation laws, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Error Estimates For Vector Field Interpolation Based On Generalized Matrix-valued Kernels
authors: Zhengjie Sun, Lishuo Dong, Leevan Ling
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Matrix-valued kernels provide a flexible framework for approximating vector fields from scattered data, especially when structural constraints such as divergence-free or curl-free conditions must be preserved. Classical potential-based constructions enforce these constraints naturally, but they typically require the generating scalar function to possess relatively high smoothness. We develop an operator-based framework for constructing div-free and curl-free matrix-valued kernels using integral and differential operators, which substantially relaxes the regularity requirements of the potential approach. Using dimension-walking techniques, we show that the resulting native spaces are norm-equivalent to appropriate vector-valued Sobolev spaces. Another main contribution of the paper is a sharp error analysis for the corresponding kernel matrix-valued interpolation problem. We derive direct Sobolev error estimates that allow fractional regularity of the target field, and we establish Bernstein-type inequalities for the associated kernel trial spaces. These results lead to a complete inverse theorem. We also investigate stability by proving lower bounds for the smallest eigenvalues of the interpolation matrices. Numerical experiments are included to verify the theoretical results.
tldr: This paper develops an operator-based framework for constructing divergence-free and curl-free matrix-valued kernels for vector field interpolation, with error analysis and stability results.
motivation: The paper addresses the need for flexible and efficient interpolation of vector fields with structural constraints, relaxing regularity requirements of classical potential-based methods.
method: The authors use integral and differential operators to construct matrix-valued kernels, employ dimension-walking techniques to show norm equivalence to Sobolev spaces, and derive Sobolev error estimates and Bernstein-type inequalities.
result: They provide sharp error estimates allowing fractional regularity, establish inverse theorems, and prove lower bounds for smallest eigenvalues of interpolation matrices, with numerical verification.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a more general and efficient approach to divergence-free and curl-free interpolation, with rigorous theoretical guarantees.

title: Fixed-Point Characterisations Of Extremal Distributions Under Partial Distributional Constraints
authors: Rabiu Tsoho Muhammad Kizito Salako
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a methodological framework for solving robust inference problems with partially specified distributions over measurable subsets of a parameter space. Partial specifications define a set of admissible distributions. The goal is to determine extremal values (over these admissible distributions) for statistical quantities, where these quantities---these objective functions---are ratios of expectations of analytic functions, continuous functions, piecewise continuous functions, and uniform limits of piecewise continuous functions. We show that extremal values are approached by sequences of admissible distributions, whose limiting extremal distributions are characterised by fixed-point conditions on their support locations. This characterises where extremal distributions place probability mass and yields a practical computational framework for solving the corresponding optimisation problems. We establish convergence and asymptotic properties of the resulting extremal distributions and extremal objective function values. This work extends robust inference methods (e.g. robust Bayesian inference) by combining extremal-distribution reduction, fixed-point characterisation, and approximation-based analysis within a unified framework.
tldr: This paper presents a methodological framework for robust inference with partially specified distributions, using fixed-point characterizations to find extremal distributions.
motivation: The authors aim to solve robust inference problems where only partial distributional constraints are known, extending methods like robust Bayesian inference.
method: They define admissible distributions based on partial specifications and characterize extremal distributions via fixed-point conditions on support locations, using approximation-based analysis.
result: They establish convergence and asymptotic properties of extremal distributions and objective function values, providing a computational framework.
conclusion: The work offers a unified framework for extremal-distribution reduction and fixed-point characterization in robust inference, but it is not related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A Linearly Convergent Projection-Free Algorithm For Smooth Convex Sets
authors: Elad Hazan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider minimizing a smooth, strongly convex function over a convex set. Projected gradient descent is known to converge linearly in this setting, but each iteration requires a projection onto the feasible set, which may be computationally expensive. We show that when the feasible set is smooth, projection can be replaced by one gradient computation and a single supporting-tangent computation per iteration, while preserving linear convergence. Moreover, the required tangent can be approximated to sufficient accuracy using [MATH] membership-oracle queries, where [MATH] is the ambient dimension. Previously, projection-free linear convergence was known only for polyhedral sets or for sets that are both smooth and strongly convex.
tldr: This paper presents a projection-free algorithm for minimizing smooth strongly convex functions over smooth convex sets, achieving linear convergence with reduced per-iteration cost.
motivation: Projected gradient descent converges linearly but requires expensive projections; the goal is to replace projections with cheaper operations while maintaining convergence.
method: The algorithm replaces projection with a single gradient computation and a supporting-tangent computation, which can be approximated using membership-oracle queries.
result: It achieves linear convergence for smooth convex sets, extending previous results that only held for polyhedral or smooth and strongly convex sets.
conclusion: The work provides a more efficient optimization method for smooth convex constraints, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum systems.

title: Kubo Ando Means On The Cone Of J Hermitian Matrices
authors: Hayden Tyler Sebastian Micalizzi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The theory of Kubo-Ando means provides a fundamental correspondence between operator means and operator monotone functions on the positive half-line. In this paper, we first extend this theory to the cone of positive quaternionic Hermitian matrices, establishing quaternionic analogues of the main results of Kubo and Ando. We then develop an analogous framework for the cone of J-Hermitian positive matrices associated with an indefinite inner product. In particular, we prove that Kubo-Ando means on this cone are again in one-to-one correspondence with operator monotone functions, thereby extending the classical characterization to this indefinite setting.
tldr: This paper extends Kubo-Ando operator means to quaternionic and indefinite inner product settings, focusing on mathematical structure rather than quantum information applications.
motivation: The paper aims to generalize the theory of Kubo-Ando means to new mathematical contexts, potentially relevant to quantum information but not directly connected.
method: The authors develop quaternionic analogues of Kubo-Ando results and extend the framework to J-Hermitian positive matrices, proving a correspondence with operator monotone functions.
result: They establish that Kubo-Ando means on the cone of J-Hermitian positive matrices are in one-to-one correspondence with operator monotone functions, extending the classical characterization.
conclusion: The work is a mathematical contribution with potential future applications, but it does not directly address the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Strong Convergence For Countable Generalized Bregman Nonexpansive-type Mappings With Equilibrium And Variational Inequality Constraints
authors: Markjoe O. Uba
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a Legendre--Bregman outer-approximation method for a common-solution problem in a uniformly smooth and uniformly convex Banach space. The constraint system consists of countable families of fixed-point-type mappings, equilibrium bifunctions, and monotone variational-inequality operators. Strong convergence to the Bregman projection of the initial point onto the common solution set is obtained without a family-level NST compatibility condition. A localized theorem covers negative-entropy generators, and Hilbert-space and Alber-functional cases are also derived.
tldr: This paper develops a Legendre-Bregman outer-approximation method for solving a common-solution problem involving fixed-point mappings, equilibrium bifunctions, and variational inequalities in Banach spaces.
motivation: The paper aims to solve a common-solution problem in Banach spaces, which is a topic in nonlinear analysis and optimization, not directly related to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
method: The method uses Legendre-Bregman projections and outer-approximation techniques to iteratively find a common solution, with strong convergence guarantees.
result: Strong convergence to the Bregman projection of the initial point is achieved without a family-level NST compatibility condition, and specialized cases are derived.
conclusion: The paper contributes to the theory of Bregman methods in Banach spaces, but it has no connection to quantum information or related fields.

title: An Adaptive Split-combine Gaussian Mixture Filter For Nonlinear And Multimodal State Estimation
authors: San Kim (department Of Brain And Cognitive Sciences, KAIST, Daejeon, Republic Of Korea), Won Chang (department Of Statistics, Seoul National University, Seoul, Republic Of Korea, The Institute For Data Innovation In Science, Seoul National University, Seoul, Republic Of Korea), Daniel B. Forger (department Of Mathematics, University Of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA, Department Of Computational Medicine And Bioinformatics, University Of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA), Dae Wook Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Filtering combines model predictions with measurements to estimate the probability density function (PDF) of a system state over time. The PDF often becomes highly asymmetric and even multimodal in nonlinear systems with oscillatory or chaotic dynamics. Such non-Gaussian features violate the single-Gaussian assumption underlying Kalman-type filters. To address this problem, Gaussian mixture filtering has been proposed. However, accurately propagating mixture components and adaptively adjusting their number and weights over time remain open challenges. Here, we develop an adaptive split-combine Gaussian mixture filter (AMF) that estimates the time evolution of asymmetric and multimodal PDFs by adaptively splitting and combining Gaussian particles without auxiliary online numerical optimization. Notably, the proposed splitting method guarantees a reduction in variance along a target level-set-point direction of a Gaussian particle. This enables accurate and efficient propagation of particles. We show that AMF consistently outperforms various baseline filters across diverse benchmarks, including single and coupled slow-fast Van der Pol oscillators and the Lorenz attractor. We also propose a parallel implementation of AMF, allowing high-fidelity PDF estimation with practical computational cost.
tldr: This paper presents an adaptive split-combine Gaussian mixture filter for nonlinear and multimodal state estimation, with applications to oscillatory and chaotic systems.
motivation: Kalman-type filters assume Gaussianity, which fails for nonlinear systems with asymmetric and multimodal probability density functions. The authors aim to improve Gaussian mixture filtering by adaptively adjusting the number and weights of components without online optimization.
method: The proposed adaptive mixture filter (AMF) splits and combines Gaussian particles based on a variance-reduction guarantee along a target level-set-point direction, and includes a parallel implementation for computational efficiency.
result: AMF consistently outperforms baseline filters on benchmarks including Van der Pol oscillators and the Lorenz attractor, achieving high-fidelity PDF estimation with practical computational cost.
conclusion: The AMF provides an accurate and efficient approach for state estimation in nonlinear and multimodal systems, with potential for parallelization.

title: A Counterexample To Fourier Alignment In Single-Neuron Modular Addition
authors: Gautam Neelakantan Memana
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a negative solution to MAIS-O60. We first construct an example in which an initially active ReLU neuron becomes completely inactive in finite time and thereafter remains frozen at a limit whose Fourier energy is equally distributed among all nonzero real frequency classes. The counterexample holds on an open set of initial conditions and therefore occurs with positive probability under Gaussian initialization. An appendix prepared by GPT-5.6 Sol strengthens the counterexample by showing that the same failure can occur for every Clarke trajectory from an open set of initial conditions, under the convention [MATH], for smooth dead-zone approximations of ReLU, and for fixed-step full-batch gradient descent. Thus, single-frequency alignment is not a general consequence of training a single neuron on modular addition.
tldr: This paper provides a counterexample to Fourier alignment in single-neuron modular addition, showing that a ReLU neuron can become inactive and its Fourier energy spread across all frequencies.
motivation: The paper addresses a specific open problem (MAIS-O60) about whether single neurons trained on modular addition align to a single frequency, which is relevant to understanding neural network learning dynamics.
method: The authors construct a specific example where a ReLU neuron becomes inactive and its Fourier energy is uniformly distributed, and they extend this to Clarke trajectories and smooth approximations using gradient descent.
result: The counterexample holds on an open set of initial conditions, indicating that single-frequency alignment is not a general consequence of training on modular addition.
conclusion: The paper concludes that Fourier alignment is not guaranteed for single-neuron modular addition, contradicting previous expectations.

title: Jointly Sparse Blind Deconvolution Via Riemannian Optimization
authors: Wenlong Wang, Baiyang Guo, Zai Yang, Shixiang Chen, Junpeng Shi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04465v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Blind deconvolution has been widely applied in system identification and signal processing. While joint sparsity commonly arises in practical scenarios, effectively exploiting this structure to enhance recovery performance remains a challenging and largely open problem. In this paper, we propose a joint-sparsity-promoting optimization problem and develop a Riemannian optimization algorithm for its accurate and efficient solution. We further establish theoretical guarantees that characterize the non-asymptotic relationship between the estimation error and the sample complexity, showing that exploiting joint sparsity can significantly reduce the sample complexity required for successful recovery. Numerical experiments are provided that validate the theoretical results and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
tldr: This paper proposes a Riemannian optimization algorithm for jointly sparse blind deconvolution, with theoretical guarantees on sample complexity.
motivation: Blind deconvolution is important in signal processing, and exploiting joint sparsity can improve recovery, but it remains challenging.
method: The authors formulate a joint-sparsity-promoting optimization problem and develop a Riemannian optimization algorithm to solve it efficiently.
result: They provide non-asymptotic theoretical guarantees showing that joint sparsity reduces sample complexity, and validate with numerical experiments.
conclusion: The proposed method effectively exploits joint sparsity for blind deconvolution, improving recovery performance.

title: Consistent Community Recovery In Stochastic Block Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Processes
authors: Almut E. D. Veraart Anders Norlyk
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose the stochastic block Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (SBOU) process, a continuous-time multivariate model in which the drift matrix encodes a latent group structure among its components. Our main contribution is a community-detection algorithm whose misclassification proportion converges to zero in a regime combining infill, long-span, and high-dimensional asymptotics. To our knowledge, this is the first consistency result of this kind for latent group recovery in a discretely observed continuous-time multivariate model. As a key intermediate result, we establish consistency of the discretely observed maximum likelihood estimator of the drift matrix in the same regime, thereby extending the high-dimensional L\'evy-driven Ornstein-Uhlenbeck literature. For practical implementation, we develop a feasible model-selection procedure for estimating the support of the drift matrix, which enables data-driven selection of the number of latent groups. The SBOU framework can be viewed as a continuous-time generalisation of the discrete-time stochastic-block VAR model, allowing for both positive and negative dynamic interactions between groups as opposed to only positive. We illustrate the methodology on the RE-Europe wind-capacity dataset and recover a country-level grouping consistent with the geographic benchmark.
tldr: This paper proposes a stochastic block Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process for community detection in continuous-time multivariate data, with consistency results under high-dimensional asymptotics.
motivation: The authors aim to extend community detection to continuous-time models, which is a novel contribution in statistics and machine learning, but not related to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.
method: They introduce a stochastic block Ornstein-Uhlenbeck model and develop a community-detection algorithm based on maximum likelihood estimation of the drift matrix, with a model-selection procedure for support estimation.
result: They prove consistency of the misclassification proportion and of the drift estimator under infill, long-span, and high-dimensional asymptotics, and illustrate on wind-capacity data.
conclusion: The work provides a new statistical framework for latent group recovery in continuous-time processes, but it is outside the scope of the user's research interests.

title: Bernoulli--Strang--Fix Conditions: Approximation And Prediction By Sampling Kantorovich Operators
authors: A. Antony Selvan Sreya T
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the Bernoulli--Strang--Fix conditions and their generalized versions for a vector-valued generator [MATH] and a periodic nonuniform sampling set [MATH]. We use these conditions to establish exact and asymptotic polynomial reproduction properties of sampling Kantorovich operators associated with [MATH] up to a prescribed degree. We analyze the approximation properties and convergence behavior of these operators in detail. Furthermore, we demonstrate their application to signal prediction from a finite number of past local average samples, showing that sampling Kantorovich operators can also serve as effective prediction operators. Finally, we present numerical examples based on Gaussian functions and B-splines to illustrate and validate the theoretical approximation and prediction results.
tldr: This paper introduces Bernoulli–Strang–Fix conditions for sampling Kantorovich operators, focusing on polynomial reproduction and signal prediction, which is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to extend classical Strang–Fix theory to sampling Kantorovich operators with vector-valued generators and nonuniform sampling sets, enabling exact polynomial reproduction and prediction.
method: They define Bernoulli–Strang–Fix conditions and generalized versions, then use them to prove exact and asymptotic polynomial reproduction properties. They also analyze approximation and convergence, and apply the operators to signal prediction from local averages.
result: The paper establishes theoretical conditions for polynomial reproduction and demonstrates the operators' effectiveness in prediction, with numerical examples using Gaussian and B-spline generators.
conclusion: Sampling Kantorovich operators satisfying the new conditions can serve as both approximation and prediction tools, validated by numerical experiments.

title: An Inverse Theorem For Partially Symmetric Two-Dimensional Semiclassical Schr\"odinger Operators
authors: Kuo Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a formal local inverse spectral result for a two-dimensional semiclassical Schr\"odinger operator whose potential well possesses a single reflection symmetry. After a harmonic linear normalization, the potential can be written as [MATH], with [MATH]. The operator can be brought into a quantum Birkhoff normal form whose Weyl symbol is a formal series [MATH]. If the coefficient [MATH] of the cubic term [MATH] is non-zero, then the first two layers of the quantum Birkhoff normal form (i.e., the coefficients [MATH] and [MATH]) uniquely determine the full Taylor series of [MATH], once the sign of [MATH] and the transverse-line data [MATH] are prescribed.
tldr: This paper proves a formal local inverse spectral result for a two-dimensional semiclassical Schrödinger operator with a single reflection symmetry, showing that the first two layers of the quantum Birkhoff normal form determine the full Taylor series of the potential under certain conditions.
motivation: The paper addresses an inverse spectral problem in semiclassical analysis, aiming to understand how much information about a potential can be recovered from spectral data.
method: The author uses quantum Birkhoff normal form and Weyl symbol techniques, along with a harmonic linear normalization, to analyze the operator's spectrum.
result: It is shown that if the cubic coefficient is non-zero, the first two layers of the normal form uniquely determine the full Taylor series of the potential, given the sign and transverse-line data.
conclusion: This contributes to the mathematical theory of inverse spectral problems, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Associative/Lie Radical (co)invariance Under Tracial (co)actions
authors: Alexandru Chirvasitu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a number of Jacobson/solvable/nilpotent-radical (co)invariance results for finite-dimensional associative or Lie (co)module-algebras over Hopf algebras [MATH], provided the characteristic, if positive, is large relative to the dimension of the algebra and the (co)actions satisfy trace-preservation conditions automatic when [MATH] is involutory. This generalizes a number of such radical-invariance criteria in the literature, due to A. Gordienko, V. Linchenko, Pagon-Repov{}-Zaicev and others, providing a uniform enriched-categorical framework for those results.
tldr: This paper proves radical (co)invariance results for finite-dimensional associative or Lie (co)module-algebras over Hopf algebras under trace-preserving conditions.
motivation: The paper aims to generalize existing radical-invariance criteria in the literature by providing a uniform enriched-categorical framework.
method: The author uses enriched category theory and Hopf algebra actions to establish Jacobson/solvable/nilpotent-radical invariance under trace-preserving (co)actions.
result: The paper proves several radical (co)invariance results for finite-dimensional algebras, generalizing prior work by Gordienko, Linchenko, Pagon-Repov-Zaicev, etc.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for radical invariance, but it is purely algebraic and not connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Isometric Composition Operators On $bmoa$ For $0<p<\infty$
authors: Zhaopeng Lin, Yufeng Lu, Chao Zu
abstract:
ArXiv:2608.04880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize the analytic self-maps of the unit disk inducing isometric composition operators on \(\BMOA\) with respect to the M\"obius-invariant \(H^p\) norm for \(p\ge1\) and the corresponding quasi-norm for \(0

<1\). Our result extends the work of Laitila for \(p=2\), Pouliasis for \(1\le p<2\), and Chen and Wulan for \(1\le p\le4\). For \(p>4\), condition in the theorem of Chen and Wulan is no longer valid. We identify an appropriate replacement and obtain equivalent characterizations valid for every \(0

<\infty\). In particular, the class of analytic symbols inducing isometric composition operators is independent of the exponent \(p\in(0,\infty)\).
tldr: This paper characterizes analytic self-maps of the unit disk that induce isometric composition operators on BMOA with respect to Möbius-invariant H^p norms for all p>0.
motivation: The study extends previous characterizations for specific p values to all p>0, correcting a condition for p>4.
method: The authors use functional analysis and complex analysis techniques to analyze composition operators on BMOA spaces with H^p norms.
result: They provide equivalent characterizations valid for every p in (0,∞), showing the class of symbols is independent of p.
conclusion: The work completes the characterization for all p, but it is in pure mathematics with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: SoK: How Frontier Ai Reshapes System-Level Security Risk Dynamics In Critical Infrastructure
authors: Chandra Thapa, Mohan Baruwal Chhetri, Marthie Grobler, Shahroz Tariq, Tooba Aamir
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frontier artificial intelligence (FAI), encompassing large-scale, general-purpose AI systems, including large language models, multimodal foundation models, and agentic systems, is increasingly integrated into critical infrastructure (CI). This challenges long-standing security assumptions of bounded behavior, segmented networks, component transparency, and human-paced decision-making. Existing AI-security literature typically organizes risks by attack type, lifecycle stage, or asset class, but fails to capture the system-level dynamics, such as how risk emerges, spreads, and is controlled, through which FAI reshapes CI security outcomes. This Systematization of Knowledge (SoK) introduces a five-dimensional risk-dynamics framework that characterizes how FAI reconfigures CI security across the lifecycle: (i) Capability Emergence through new FAI-enabled attack and defense capabilities, (ii) Infiltration Pathways through data, models and AI supply chains, (iii) Cross-System Propagation across interconnected infrastructures and dependencies, (iv) degradation of effective technical and human Control Authority, and (v) strain on institutional Response Capacity under operational pressure. Rather than enumerating threats, the framework identifies recurring mechanisms that jointly determine system-level risk. We further identify a structural mismatch between academic AI-security research and CI operational constraints, and derive a deployment-oriented research agenda grounded in system-level assurance criteria. Collectively, this work shifts attention from model-centric robustness to lifecycle-structured, system-level assurance in interconnected CI environments.
tldr: This SoK paper analyzes how frontier AI reshapes security risk dynamics in critical infrastructure, proposing a five-dimensional framework.
motivation: Existing AI-security literature fails to capture system-level risk dynamics in critical infrastructure when frontier AI is integrated.
method: The authors introduce a five-dimensional risk-dynamics framework covering capability emergence, infiltration pathways, cross-system propagation, control authority degradation, and response capacity strain.
result: They identify a structural mismatch between academic AI-security research and CI operational constraints, and propose a deployment-oriented research agenda.
conclusion: The paper shifts focus from model-centric robustness to lifecycle-structured, system-level assurance in interconnected CI environments.

title: When Modalities Fail To Tango: Conformal Backdoor Detection In Multimodal Contrastive Learning
authors: Yiming Chen, Kemou Li, Haiwei Wu, Jiantao Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Backdoor attacks in multimodal contrastive learning (MCL) have garnered growing attention in recent years, as many downstream tasks critically depend on pre-trained MCL models. Existing detection-based defenses predominantly rely on the CLIPScore metric, under the assumption that poisoned pairs exhibit lower semantic similarity between the image and the caption. However, we identify two critical flaws remaining in existing methods: (1) the substantial overlap between CLIPScore distributions of benign and poisoned pairs undermines the reliability of this metric, and (2) fixed-threshold detection cannot provide statistical guarantees for ambiguous samples within overlapping regions. To overcome these limitations, we propose integrating conformal prediction (CP), a statistical framework that quantifies uncertainty through nonconformity scores (NCSs), to establish provable confidence bounds for detecting poisoned image-caption pairs. Building on CP, we introduce CASCADE, a novel two-stage Coarse-to-Fine Conformal Backdoor Detection framework. The coarse-grained stage uses cross-modality consistency to identify high-confidence benign and poisoned pairs. In the fine-grained stage, a reference set is constructed from high-confidence poisoned pairs, and instance-level NCSs based on text-space similarity are computed for each sample in the unidentified subset. These NCSs measure conformity to the poisoning distribution and enable precise identification of latent poisoned pairs within the unidentified subset. Extensive experiments on the large-scale CC3M dataset demonstrate that CASCADE achieves an average FPR of 5.79% at 100% TPR and an average AUROC of 0.9867 across diverse attacks, while remaining effective against adaptive attacks.
tldr: This paper proposes a conformal prediction-based backdoor detection framework for multimodal contrastive learning, focusing on security of pre-trained models.
motivation: Existing backdoor detection methods in multimodal contrastive learning rely on CLIPScore with fixed thresholds, which fail due to overlapping score distributions and lack statistical guarantees.
method: CASCADE uses a two-stage approach: coarse-grained filtering via cross-modality consistency, then fine-grained detection using nonconformity scores based on text-space similarity to identify poisoned pairs with conformal confidence bounds.
result: Experiments on CC3M show high detection performance (FPR 5.79% at 100% TPR, AUROC 0.9867) and robustness against adaptive attacks.
conclusion: The framework provides statistically guaranteed backdoor detection in multimodal contrastive learning, addressing limitations of prior methods.

title: AgentAntibody: An Adaptive Immune System For Defending Llm Agents Against Prompt Injection
authors: Shihao Weng, Yang Feng, Xiaofei Xie, Jiongchi Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prompt injection remains a critical threat to LLM agents, yet existing defenses treat each task as a self-contained problem, independent of previous encounters. In practice, user requests are often underspecified: they describe the desired outcome without fully specifying acceptable behavior. An injection can exploit this ambiguity, causing the agent to complete the task in a way the user would reject. As the user's expectations become clearer through concrete cases, a defense should learn from each encounter and apply what it learns to the next. Inspired by adaptive immunity, we propose AgentAntibody, which equips LLM agents with a self-evolving immune system against prompt injection. AgentAntibody represents its evolving understanding of the user's security boundary as a persistent library of antibodies. At runtime, the library recognizes threats to this boundary and mounts corresponding immune responses. Across encounters, it evolves to strengthen the agent's immunity to future attacks. Extensive experiments across three benchmarks and four backbone LLMs show that, by learning the user's boundary through experience, AgentAntibody outperforms existing defenses in preventing harmful actions while preserving legitimate task completion, even when the harmful and legitimate actions are both compatible with the stated task.
tldr: This paper proposes an adaptive immune system for defending LLM agents against prompt injection attacks.
motivation: Existing defenses treat each task independently, failing to learn from past encounters, while user requests are often underspecified, allowing injections to exploit ambiguity.
method: AgentAntibody maintains a persistent library of antibodies representing the user's security boundary, which evolves over time to recognize and respond to threats.
result: Experiments across three benchmarks and four LLMs show it outperforms existing defenses in preventing harmful actions while preserving legitimate task completion.
conclusion: Learning the user's security boundary through experience improves defense against prompt injection without sacrificing task performance.

title: An Inline Control Architecture For Language Models In Intelligent Transportation Systems
authors: Mounira Msahli Narendra Kumar Dewangan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) systems increasingly incorporate large language models (LLMs) for semantic tasks such as message summarization, operator assistance, and decision support at roadside units and edge nodes. Although these components are not part of safety-critical control loops, they introduce prompt-level attack surfaces that are not addressed by traditional V2X security mechanisms focused on authentication and message integrity. This paper presents Guarded-V2X, an inline semantic guardrail architecture for securing LLM-enabled V2X services under real-time constraints. The proposed system integrates rule-based ingress filtering, a lightweight safety classifier, policy-constrained structured generation, trusted-only retrieval, and post-decision adjudication to enforce machine-checkable safety boundaries prior to downstream execution. Guarded-V2X is evaluated using a four-stage experimental pipeline encompassing intrusion vulnerability analysis, calibration and latency benchmarking, guardrail validation, and robustness under adversarial stress. Experiments are conducted on a V2X-aligned simulated dataset derived from RSU advisories, operator messages, and annotated V2X message summaries. Results show that unguarded and prompt-only baselines retain residual vulnerability under multi-turn adversarial trials, while Guarded-V2X consistently reduces intrusion acceptance success rates and eliminates observed unsafe completions in two-turn settings, without exceeding latency budgets for V2X semantic advisory paths.
tldr: This paper presents Guarded-V2X, an inline semantic guardrail architecture for securing LLM-enabled V2X services, focusing on prompt-level attack surfaces.
motivation: V2X systems increasingly use LLMs for semantic tasks, introducing prompt-level attack surfaces not addressed by traditional security mechanisms.
method: The proposed system integrates rule-based ingress filtering, a lightweight safety classifier, policy-constrained structured generation, trusted-only retrieval, and post-decision adjudication.
result: Experiments show Guarded-V2X reduces intrusion acceptance success rates and eliminates unsafe completions in two-turn settings without exceeding latency budgets.
conclusion: The architecture provides a practical solution for securing LLM-enabled V2X services under real-time constraints.

title: Sublogarithmic Swap Regret In Multiplayer General-Sum Games Via Hybrid Regularization
authors: Taira Tsuchiya
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Swap regret governs the rate at which uncoupled learning dynamics converge to correlated equilibria in multiplayer general-sum games. Under full-information feedback, the best previous guarantee when every player follows the same dynamics grows logarithmically in the horizon [MATH]. We construct uncoupled dynamics under which every player incurs only [MATH] swap regret, where [MATH] is the number of players and [MATH] bounds the number of actions per player. To our knowledge, this is the first sublogarithmic individual guarantee in this setting, and it implies that the time-averaged product distribution of play is an [MATH]-approximate correlated equilibrium. The key algorithmic choice is to combine the Blum--Mansour reduction with optimistic follow-the-regularized-leader using a hybrid regularizer that separately weights negative Shannon entropy and the log-barrier: the entropy controls the optimistic prediction error, whereas the log-barrier controls the transition-matrix movement through its Bregman divergence. A new sensitivity theorem for stationary distributions of Markov chains, which involves neither mixing parameters nor the smallest transition probability, transfers this control to the played strategies and yields a simpler analysis without local-norm or self-concordance arguments. The guarantee is preserved by an adversarially robust variant that additionally ensures [MATH] swap regret against arbitrary utility sequences, and by a horizon-free variant that requires no prior knowledge of [MATH].
tldr: This paper presents a new algorithm achieving sublogarithmic swap regret in multiplayer general-sum games, a result in algorithmic game theory.
motivation: The paper aims to improve the convergence rate of learning dynamics to correlated equilibria in multiplayer games, which is a fundamental question in game theory and online learning.
method: The method combines the Blum-Mansour reduction with optimistic follow-the-regularized-leader using a hybrid regularizer that weights negative Shannon entropy and the log-barrier, and introduces a new sensitivity theorem for stationary distributions of Markov chains.
result: The algorithm achieves the first sublogarithmic individual swap regret guarantee, implying an approximate correlated equilibrium, and is robust to adversarial utility sequences and horizon-free.

title: Topological Semantics For Scoped Computational Paths
authors: Arthur Freitas Ramos, Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz, Anjolina Grisi de Oliveira, Tiago M. L. de Veras
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computational paths record equality as explicit finite traces of primitive steps. We give a topological semantics for a scoped rewrite presentation whose steps have continuous geometric realizations and whose named rewrites carry endpoint-fixed homotopies. For every presentation we construct a quotient arrow space with a canonical final-domain groupoid structure: multiplication is continuous on the quotient of explicitly composable representatives. We prove an exact four-way criterion for this final composable topology to agree with the ordinary pullback topology, together with a compact-Hausdorff sufficient condition. Thus the unconditional construction exposes, rather than hides, the product-quotient issue in ordinary topological groupoids. The realization map to geometric homotopy classes is a continuous groupoid morphism and is faithful exactly under a separate geometric-completeness condition. In the universal presentation, a continuous section identifies the coherent-path quotient homeomorphically with the usual quotient-topologized fundamental groupoid. We then give finite-generator circle and genuine torus examples, with winding-based normal forms and classifications by Z and Z^2. A Lean 4.24.0 development checks the theorem package; the mathematical presentation is independent of the implementation.
tldr: This paper presents a topological semantics for scoped computational paths, constructing quotient arrow spaces with groupoid structures and proving conditions for topology agreement.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a rigorous topological framework for computational paths, which record equality as explicit traces, and to address the product-quotient issue in topological groupoids.
method: They define a scoped rewrite presentation with continuous geometric realizations, construct a quotient arrow space with a canonical final-domain groupoid structure, and prove criteria for topology agreement using compact-Hausdorff conditions.
result: They prove an exact four-way criterion for the final composable topology to agree with the ordinary pullback topology, and show that the realization map is a continuous groupoid morphism, faithful under a geometric-completeness condition. They also provide examples with winding-based normal forms.
conclusion: The work offers a novel topological semantics for computational paths, with potential applications in homotopy type theory and formal verification, but it is not directly related to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Trident : How To Break Deep Reinforcement Learning Cyber Defenses (Agentic)
authors: Ryozo Masukawa, Ian Bryant, Armita Kazeminajafabadi, Sanggeon Yun, Hyunwoo Oh, Sungheon Jeong, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Mahdi Imani, Mohsen Imani
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous cyber defense systems based on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) have attracted significant research attention, yet remain evaluated almost exclusively against static, heuristic red agents, leaving their robustness against adaptive threats critically understudied. Meanwhile, recent advances in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) have improved LLM reasoning, but their integration into cybersecurity remains elusive due to the absence of suitable benchmark environments and interaction datasets. To bridge this gap, we introduce Trident, an agentic LLM red teaming framework comprising three components: a dynamic benchmark with isolated sandbox servers spanning CybORG CAGE 4 and CyberWheel, a dataset comprises over 13,000 high-fidelity red-blue interaction trajectories for RLVR, and a ``Code-as-Policy'' RLVR agentic architecture Trident Agentic). The latter reformulates red agent training as a contextual bandit via a tripartite Log Summarizer--Planner--Coder design, where a trainable Planner generates complete attack strategies from compressed execution logs, which a frozen Coder translates into executable Python policies deployed against live DRL defenders. Empirical evaluations reveal a fundamental brittleness in existing defenses: with a single trainable 7B planner, Trident reduces blue agent defensive performance by an average of 522% compared to static red agent baselines while autonomously discovering emergent behaviors such as decoy avoidance and adaptive state prioritization that static heuristics entirely fail to uncover.
tldr: This paper introduces Trident, an agentic LLM red teaming framework that uses reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to attack deep reinforcement learning-based cyber defenses, revealing their brittleness.
motivation: Existing autonomous cyber defense systems are evaluated only against static heuristics, leaving their robustness against adaptive threats understudied. The authors aim to bridge this gap by integrating recent advances in LLM reasoning into cybersecurity.
method: Trident comprises a dynamic benchmark with sandbox servers, a dataset of over 13,000 red-blue interaction trajectories, and a 'Code-as-Policy' RLVR agentic architecture with a Log Summarizer-Planner-Coder design. A trainable Planner generates attack strategies from logs, which a frozen Coder translates into executable Python policies.
result: With a single trainable 7B planner, Trident reduces blue agent defensive performance by an average of 522% compared to static red agents, and discovers emergent behaviors like decoy avoidance and adaptive state prioritization.
conclusion: The findings highlight fundamental brittleness in current DRL-based cyber defenses and demonstrate the potential of agentic LLMs for red teaming, but the work is not aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Breadcrumbing Search Agents
authors: Xuebin Li, Hanqing Zhao, Siyuan Liang, Kejiang Chen, Weiming Zhang, Dacheng Tao, Nenghai Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based search agents are widely used for information-seeking tasks, but their reliance on external tool returns introduces a critical security risk: web content retrieved during execution is untrusted, exposing agents to prompt injection and goal hijacking. Prior work on search-agent safety primarily focuses on static web-content injection, but modern agents issue follow-up queries and cross-check competing sources, so a single injected page is often diluted or rejected. We show that the channel delivering search and page observations is a fragile security boundary: beyond exposing the agent to a single poisoned page, a mediated search interface can repeatedly steer how the agent gathers evidence and forms its final answer. Under a constrained tool-intermediary threat model, appending only one controlled result per query can substantially increase attack success when the evidence is coordinated across the agent's trajectory. We study this setting with a strategy-driven long-horizon attack system and introduce Authority-Chain Hijack (ACH), an expert-refined strategy that turns isolated search-result and page-content manipulations into a coherent evidence chain across seemingly corroborating sources. ACH achieves the highest Overall ASR among all baselines, reaching 55.9% / 83.3% ASR / MaxN ASR on the full SafeSearch test split. We further introduce Trace-Guided Strategy Evolution (TGSE), which automatically improves attacker strategies from execution traces, replacing manual redesign with trace-driven refinement; its strongest single setting reaches 71.4% / 95.0% in held-out evaluation.
tldr: This paper introduces a novel attack system for LLM-based search agents, demonstrating that coordinated manipulation of search results can hijack the agent's evidence chain and final answer.
motivation: LLM-based search agents are vulnerable to prompt injection and goal hijacking via untrusted web content, and prior defenses assume static single-page attacks. The authors aim to show that a mediated search interface can repeatedly steer the agent across its trajectory, increasing attack success.
method: The authors propose Authority-Chain Hijack (ACH), an expert-refined strategy that coordinates isolated search-result and page-content manipulations into a coherent evidence chain across seemingly corroborating sources. They also introduce Trace-Guided Strategy Evolution (TGSE) to automatically improve attacker strategies from execution traces.
result: ACH achieves the highest Overall ASR among baselines, reaching 55.9% / 83.3% ASR / MaxN ASR on the full SafeSearch test split. TGSE's strongest single setting reaches 71.4% / 95.0% in held-out evaluation.
conclusion: The work highlights a critical security boundary in search-agent pipelines and demonstrates that coordinated, trajectory-level attacks are highly effective, urging the need for more robust defenses.

title: Adaptive Intrusion Detection System Using Transformer-Based Neural Networks And Continual Learning Approach With Adversarial Investigation
authors: Azizi Ariffin, Afif Haris, Faiz Zaki, Hazim Hanif, Nor Badrul Anuar
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Network intrusion detection systems (IDS) trained on fixed traffic snapshots decay silently after deployment as threat distributions shift. Fine-tuning models on new attacks triggers catastrophic forgetting, while retraining from scratch is computationally infeasible. Replay-based continual learning counters this, but existing methods unrealistically confine benign traffic to a single early task and ignore the replay buffer as a potential attack surface. To address this, we present an adaptive IDS framework coupling a tabular transformer encoder with a class balanced experience replay buffer that replays benign traffic at every update to stabilize decision boundaries. We introduce the class-instance incremental (CII) scenario where benign flows reappear alongside new attacks as a more faithful stress test, and probe the buffer with overt label flipping and stealthy backdoor poisoning attacks. On the CICIDS2017 benchmark, our framework achieved 0.9994 accuracy under the traditional class incremental setup and 0.9989 under CII, with negligible forgetting, drastically outperforming sequential fine-tuning (0.0052), EWC (0.0324), LwF (0.0699), and iCaRL (0.8770) baselines. While injecting benign traffic into every experience proves essential for preventing forgetting, the replay buffer introduces critical vulnerabilities. Label-flipping collapses the model entirely (0.0053 accuracy at a 1% budget), and the backdoor maintains 0.97 overall accuracy while driving the attack success rate on trigger flows to 95%, evading standard monitoring. Ultimately, while a modest replay budget recovers near-joint-training performance, ensuring buffer integrity emerges as a strict operational requirement.
tldr: This paper presents an adaptive network intrusion detection system using a transformer and continual learning, with a focus on replay buffer security.
motivation: Network intrusion detection systems degrade over time due to shifting threat distributions, and existing continual learning methods have unrealistic assumptions and vulnerabilities.
method: The authors propose a tabular transformer encoder with a class-balanced experience replay buffer that replays benign traffic at every update, and introduce a class-instance incremental scenario. They also probe the buffer with label flipping and backdoor attacks.
result: The framework achieves high accuracy on CICIDS2017 (0.9994 in class incremental, 0.9989 in CII), outperforming baselines, but is vulnerable to replay buffer attacks: label flipping collapses accuracy to 0.0053, and a backdoor achieves 95% attack success rate.
conclusion: Replay-based continual learning is effective for adaptive IDS, but buffer integrity is a critical operational requirement.

title: Hidden Ciphers And Where To Find Them: Static Discovery And Assessment Of Cryptographic Assets In Software
authors: Eduard Hirsch Christian N\"ather
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern software systems rely on cryptography for data protection, authentication, and trust establishment, yet organizations often lack a structured view of the cryptography deployed across source code, configuration, dependencies, and cryptographic files. This lack of visibility complicates security governance and post-quantum migration planning. This paper presents a static approach for discovering and assessing cryptographic assets in software systems. We introduce a classification of Crypto-Material, Crypto-Artifacts, and Crypto-Invocations, derive an extensible scanner-independent rule repository from it, and implement a static scanner that applies these rules to produce CBOM-oriented output. We evaluate the approach on a synthetic benchmark with known ground truth and on a real-world infrastructure of ten deployed services. The scanner achieves an F1 score of 0.75 for asset discovery and correctly annotates 91% of expected weaknesses and vulnerabilities. In the realworld setting, it processes 57 610 files in under six minutes and discovers 370 cryptographic assets, including six CVE-linked vulnerabilities and 52 post-quantum migration candidates. Real-world coverage is assessed against a manually compiled reference list rather than an exhaustive one. These results show that classification-driven static discovery can provide practical cryptographic transparency for governance and post-quantum migration planning.
tldr: This paper presents a static analysis tool for discovering and assessing cryptographic assets in software, focusing on governance and post-quantum migration planning.
motivation: Organizations lack visibility into the cryptography deployed across their software, complicating security governance and post-quantum migration planning.
method: The authors introduce a classification of Crypto-Material, Crypto-Artifacts, and Crypto-Invocations, derive a scanner-independent rule repository, and implement a static scanner that produces CBOM-oriented output.
result: The scanner achieves an F1 score of 0.75 on a synthetic benchmark, correctly annotates 91% of expected weaknesses, and processes 57,610 files in under six minutes, discovering 370 cryptographic assets including six CVE-linked vulnerabilities and 52 post-quantum migration candidates.
conclusion: Classification-driven static discovery can provide practical cryptographic transparency for governance and post-quantum migration planning.

title: LLM-Assisted Detection And Repair Of Hardware Security Vulnerabilities In Verilog Designs
authors: Ethen Santana, Gabriel Gyaase, Hao Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hardware designs, like software, are susceptible to bugs that can introduce security vulnerabilities and create opportunities for malicious exploitation. Unlike software vulnerabilities, however, hardware flaws become permanently embedded in silicon after fabrication, making them difficult or impossible to patch. The proposed approach is evaluated iteratively on a dataset of single-module Verilog designs to assess its effectiveness in detecting hardware security weaknesses. Our results demonstrate the potential of LLMs to augment traditional hardware security analysis by providing automated, scalable assistance for identifying security vulnerabilities during the hardware design process.

title: Self-sustained Electric Field-driven Off-grid Platform For On-demand Microdroplet Charging And Programmable Manipulation
authors: Jeongseok Oh And Dongwhi Choi Donghan Lee
abstract: Power independence and system simplicity are paramount for robust droplet manipulation in decentralized applications, including point-of-care diagnostics and wearable biosensors. However, conventional active microfluidics for droplet manipulation are often bottlenecked by the requirement for high-voltage power supplies, intricate electrode networks, or magnetic additives that escalate system complexity and restrict portability. Here, we report a self-sustained electric-field-based electrophoretic platform (SELF-EP) that achieves autonomous droplet charging and sophisticated manipulation, entirely eliminating the need for external power sources. This is enabled by a specialized SELF emitter engineered to retain quasi-permanent surface charges, providing a continuous and stable SELF. Rather than direct charge injection, SELF drives electrostatic induction, drawing charges from ground to induce a net charge on droplets. Through integrated theoretical modeling and experimental validation, we demonstrate that the SELF-EP allows for deterministic control of droplet charge and supports on-demand droplet manipulation with various spatial configurations. Notably, we show parallelized control of multiple droplets and realize complex, programmable functions such as self-alignment and routing via precise spatial patterning of surface charges. Our SELF-EP paradigm bypasses the need for active electronics, offering a minimalist yet multifunctional strategy that significantly expands the boundaries of autonomous microfluidic and biomedical technologies.
tldr: This paper presents a self-sustained electric-field-based platform for droplet manipulation without external power, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

result: The platform achieves deterministic droplet charging, parallelized control, and complex functions like self-alignment and routing via spatial charge patterning.
conclusion: The SELF-EP paradigm offers a minimalist, power-independent approach for autonomous microfluidics, expanding possibilities in biomedical and point-of-care applications.

title: The Astronomy Of Halakhic Nightfall: Calculating Ts'eit HaKokhavim And Motsa'ei Shabbat
authors: Aster G. Taylor
abstract: ArXiv:2608.04064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Jewish tradition, the boundary between days is not midnight, but nightfall. Nightfall is when one must pray ma'ariv, count the omer, and may engage in activity after Shabbat. While there are slightly different definitions of nightfall for Shabbat restrictions (Motsa'ei Shabbat) versus other purposes (Ts'eit HaKokhavim), most minhagim define nightfall to be when three stars of some specified size and proximity are visible in the sky. This definition presents some difficulty. Not only are these conditions difficult to define, they are further complicated by weather, cloud cover, and light pollution. Observant Jews therefore usually approximate these times by defining nightfall to be when the sun has reached a certain distance below the horizon. Although these approximations have been effective, modern astronomy enables us to calculate precisely when these conditions are met. This work applies these techniques to calculate the time of Ts'eit HaKokhavim and Motsa'ei Shabbat evaluates the accuracy of the approximations, and explores the effects of light pollution on these times. While Ts'eit HaKokhavim is reasonably well-approximated by standard methods, the conditions for Motsa'ei Shabbat generally occur after the time predicted by the approximations. Light pollution does not shift Ts'eit HaKokhavim by more than a minute but significantly changes Motsa'ei Shabbat. In fact, light pollution causes the conditions of Motsa'ei Shabbat to never be met on at least some nights in every population center. Finally, I provide a tool (halakhic-nightfall.streamlit.app) for calculating Ts'eit HaKokhavim and Motsa'ei Shabbat at an arbitrary time and location on Earth.

result: Finds standard approximations are reasonable for Ts'eit HaKokhavim but underestimate Motsa'ei Shabbat; light pollution can prevent Motsa'ei Shabbat conditions in urban areas.
conclusion: Provides a web tool for accurate nightfall calculations, highlighting the need for location-specific adjustments.

Alternative approaches have emerged in recent years based on asymmetric interferometric nonlinear cross-correlations with highly nonlinear media, and have demonstrated, for example, the field-resolved study of exciton ensembles. However, these nonlinear cross-correlation-based techniques have been benchmarked almost exclusively by self-referenced pulse characterization rather than by their quantitative spectroscopic performance, and all-optical approaches have received less attention than those based on direct charge emission. Here we extend all-optical asymmetric interferometric cross-correlation to higher nonlinearities in sub-wavelength films and demonstrate field-resolved spectroscopy of the free-induction decay of two ro-vibrational bands of ambient water vapor with a performance comparable to state of the art electro-optic sampling. The measurement spans 190 THz of bandwidth (80 THz to 270 THz) with sub-500 GHz spectral resolution, a spectral intensity dynamic range of six orders of magnitude, and a field-strength noise floor of 100 kV per meter. We anticipate the rapid adoption of here presented all-optical sampling to many experimental settings and a broad impact beyond the ultrafast optics research community as it is drastically simplified in comparison to ionization based techniques and allows the translation of electro-optic-sampling-level sensitivity into higher frequency ranges not previously accessible by conventional tools.
